quiz.q: What does K. claim to be when he is woken at night?
o: The land surveyor sent for by the Count
quiz.why_uz: U o'zini graf chaqirgan yer o'lchovchi deb ataydi.

quiz.q: How does the Castle answer on the telephone?
o: First it denies, then confirms him as land surveyor
quiz.why_uz: Avval «yer o'lchovchi yo'q», keyin «xato» — uni tan oladi.

quiz.q: What is strange about the main street of the village?
o: It leads near the Castle but never gets closer
quiz.why_uz: Ko'cha Qasrga yaqin olib boradi-yu, burilib ketadi.

chapters.title: 2. Barnabas
chapters.recap_uz: Aravakash Gerstekker K.ni chanada mehmonxonaga olib boradi. U yerda K.ni «eski yordamchilari» Artur va Yeremiya kutib turadi — ular yer o'lchashni bilishmaydi, asboblari ham yo'q. K. Qasrga telefon qiladi: «Hech qachon» degan javob oladi. Xabarchi Barnabas Klammdan maktub keltiradi: K. xizmatga qabul qilingan, boshlig'i — qishloq oqsoqoli. K. qishloq ishchisi bo'lib, Qasrga yo'l ochishga qaror qiladi.

paras.en: K. was still standing in the snow, with little desire to lift a foot out of it only to sink it again a little further on into the depth. The master tanner and his companion, satisfied at having got rid of K. for good, edged slowly back into the house through the barely opened door, constantly glancing back at K., and K. was alone with the snow that wrapped him round. 'An occasion for a little despair,' it occurred to him, 'if only I were standing here by chance and not on purpose.'
paras.uz: K. hamon qorda turardi; oyog'ini qordan ko'tarib, uni biroz nariroqda yana chuqurlikka botirishga xohishi kam edi. Ko'nchi usta va uning sherigi K.ni uzil-kesil tashqariga chiqarganlaridan mamnun bo'lib, doim K.ga orqaga qarab, ozgina ochilgan eshikdan sekin uyga kirib ketishdi va K. uni o'rab olgan qor bilan yolg'iz qoldi. «Biroz umidsizlikka tushish uchun fursat, — degan fikr keldi uning xayoliga, — agar men bu yerda ataylab emas, tasodifan turgan bo'lsam.»

paras.en: Then in the cottage on the left a tiny window opened. Closed, it had looked deep blue, perhaps from the reflection of the snow, and it was so tiny that now it was open one could not see the whole face of the person looking out, only the eyes, old brown eyes. 'There he is,' K. heard a quavering woman's voice say. 'It's the land surveyor,' said a man's voice. Then the man came to the window and asked, not unkindly, but as though he cared that everything should be in order on the road in front of his house: 'Who are you waiting for?' — 'For a sledge to take me along,' said K. 'No sledge comes this way,' said the man, 'there's no traffic here.' 'But it's the road that leads to the Castle,' K. objected. 'All the same, all the same,' said the man with a certain implacability, 'there's no traffic here.' Then both were silent. But the man was evidently turning something over, for he still kept open the window, from which smoke was pouring. 'A bad road,' said K., to help him along.
paras.uz: Shunda chap tomondagi kulbada kichkina bir deraza ochildi; yopiq paytida u, ehtimol qorning aksi tufayli, to'q ko'k ko'ringan edi va shunchalik kichkina ediki, endi ochilganida tashqariga qarayotgan odamning butun yuzi emas, faqat ko'zlari — keksa, jigarrang ko'zlar ko'rinardi. «Ana u turibdi», degan titroq ayol ovozini eshitdi K. «Bu yer o'lchovchi», dedi erkak ovozi. Keyin erkak derazaga keldi va do'stona bo'lmagan emas, lekin go'yo uyining oldidagi ko'chada hamma narsa tartibda bo'lishini istayotgandek so'radi: «Kimni kutyapsiz?» — «Meni olib ketadigan chanani», dedi K. «Bu yerdan chana o'tmaydi, — dedi erkak, — bu yerda qatnov yo'q.» «Axir bu Qasrga olib boradigan yo'l-ku», e'tiroz bildirdi K. «Baribir, baribir, — dedi erkak qandaydir qat'iylik bilan, — bu yerda qatnov yo'q.» Keyin ikkalasi ham jim qolishdi. Lekin erkak, aftidan, nimanidir o'ylardi, chunki tutun chiqib turgan derazani hamon ochiq ushlab turardi. «Yomon yo'l», dedi K. unga yordam berish uchun.

paras.en: But he only said: 'Yes, indeed.'
paras.uz: U esa faqat: «Ha, albatta», dedi.

paras.en: After a little while, though, he did say: 'If you like, I'll drive you in my sledge.' — 'Please do,' said K., delighted. 'How much do you want for it?' — 'Nothing,' said the man. K. was very surprised. 'You're the land surveyor, after all,' said the man by way of explanation, 'and you belong to the Castle. Where do you want to go?' — 'To the Castle,' said K. quickly. 'Then I won't drive you,' said the man at once. 'But I belong to the Castle,' said K., repeating the man's own words. 'Maybe,' said the man, turning him away. 'Then drive me to the inn,' said K. 'All right,' said the man, 'I'll come at once with the sledge.' The whole thing did not give the impression of any particular friendliness, but rather of a kind of very selfish, anxious, almost pedantic eagerness to remove K. from the spot in front of the house. The yard gate opened and out came a small sledge for light loads, quite flat, without any kind of seat, drawn by a feeble little horse, and behind it the man — stooping, weak, limping, with a thin, red face streaming with a cold, which looked especially small because of a woollen scarf wound tightly round his head. The man was visibly ill, and had come out only so as to be able to take K. away. K. mentioned something of the sort, but the man waved it aside. All K. learned was that he was the carter Gerstäcker, and that he had taken this uncomfortable sledge because it happened to be ready and pulling out another would have taken too long. 'Sit down,' he said, pointing with his whip to the back of the sledge. 'I'll sit beside you,' said K. 'I'll walk,' said Gerstäcker. 'But why?' asked K. 'I'll walk,' Gerstäcker repeated, and had a fit of coughing that shook him so much that he had to brace his legs in the snow and hold on to the edge of the sledge with his hands. K. said nothing more, sat down on the back of the sledge; the coughing slowly subsided, and they set off.
paras.uz: Lekin biroz o'tgach, baribir dedi: «Agar xohlasangiz, sizni chanamda olib boraman.» — «Iltimos, olib boring, — dedi K. xursand bo'lib, — buning uchun qancha so'raysiz?» — «Hech narsa», dedi erkak. K. juda hayron bo'ldi. «Axir siz yer o'lchovchisiz, — dedi erkak tushuntirib, — va Qasrga tegishlisiz. Qayerga bormoqchisiz?» — «Qasrga», dedi K. tezda. «Unda olib bormayman», dedi erkak darhol. «Axir men Qasrga tegishliman-ku», dedi K. erkakning o'z so'zlarini takrorlab. «Bo'lishi mumkin», dedi erkak rad etib. «Unda meni mehmonxonaga olib boring», dedi K. «Yaxshi, — dedi erkak, — hozir chana bilan chiqaman.» Bularning hammasi alohida do'stlik taassurotini emas, balki K.ni uy oldidagi joydan olib ketishga qaratilgan qandaydir juda xudbin, xavotirli, deyarli mayda-chuyda intilish taassurotini qoldirardi. Hovli darvozasi ochildi va yengil yuklar uchun mo'ljallangan, butunlay yassi, hech qanday o'rindiqsiz, zaif bir ot tortgan kichkina chana chiqdi, uning orqasidan esa erkak — bukchaygan, zaif, oqsoqlanib, ozg'in, qizil, tumovlagan yuzli; boshiga mahkam o'ralgan jun sharf tufayli yuzi ayniqsa kichkina ko'rinardi. Erkak ko'rinib turibdiki kasal edi va faqat K.ni olib ketish uchungina tashqariga chiqqan edi. K. shunga o'xshash nimadir dedi, lekin erkak qo'l siltadi. K. faqat uning aravakash Gerstekker ekanini va bu noqulay chanani shunchaki tayyor turgani va boshqasini chiqarish juda ko'p vaqt olgani uchun olganini bildi. «O'tiring», dedi u qamchi bilan chananing orqa qismini ko'rsatib. «Men yoningizga o'tiraman», dedi K. «Men piyoda boraman», dedi Gerstekker. «Nega?» — so'radi K. «Men piyoda boraman», takrorladi Gerstekker va uni shunchalik silkitgan yo'tal xurujiga tutildiki, oyoqlarini qorga tirab, qo'llari bilan chana chetini ushlashga majbur bo'ldi. K. boshqa hech narsa demadi, chananing orqasiga o'tirdi, yo'tal asta-sekin bosildi va ular yo'lga tushishdi.

paras.en: The Castle up there, already strangely dark, which K. had hoped to reach that very day, was moving away again. But as if he were to be given a sign by way of a provisional farewell, a bell rang out up there, a joyful, buoyant bell, which for at least a moment made the heart tremble, as though — for the sound was painful too — it were threatened with the fulfilment of what it uncertainly longed for. But soon this great bell fell silent and was replaced by a weak, monotonous little bell, perhaps still up above, but perhaps already in the village. This tinkling, of course, suited better the slow drive and the wretched but implacable carter.
paras.uz: K. bugunoq yetib borishga umid qilgan, allaqachon g'alati qorong'ilashgan tepadagi Qasr yana uzoqlashdi. Lekin go'yo unga vaqtinchalik xayrlashuv uchun baribir bir belgi berilishi kerakdek, u yerda qo'ng'iroq ovozi yangradi — quvnoq, qanotli qo'ng'iroq, u hech bo'lmaganda bir lahzaga yurakni titratdi, go'yo — chunki ovoz og'riqli ham edi — unga noaniq orzu qilgan narsasining ro'yobga chiqishi tahdid solayotgandek. Lekin tez orada bu katta qo'ng'iroq jim bo'ldi va uning o'rnini zaif, bir xil ovozli kichkina qo'ng'iroqcha egalladi — balki hali tepada, balki allaqachon qishloqda. Bu jiringlash, albatta, sekin yurish va ayanchli, lekin qat'iy aravakashga ko'proq mos kelardi.

paras.en: 'You,' K. suddenly called out — they were already near the church, the way to the inn was not far now, K. could risk something — 'I'm very surprised that you dare drive me about on your own responsibility. Are you allowed to?' Gerstäcker paid no attention and walked calmly on beside the little horse. 'Hey!' called K., scraped together some snow from the sledge and hit Gerstäcker with it full in the ear. At that he stopped and turned round; but when K. now saw him so close — the sledge had slid on a little further — this stooped, in a sense ill-treated figure, the red, tired, narrow face with its somehow unequal cheeks, one flat, the other sunken, the open, listening mouth with only a few scattered teeth in it, he had to repeat out of pity what he had said before out of malice: whether Gerstäcker might not be punished for carrying K. about. 'What do you want?' asked Gerstäcker uncomprehendingly, but did not wait for any further explanation; he called to the little horse, and they drove on again. When they were almost at the inn — K. recognized it by a bend in the road — it was to his astonishment already completely dark. Had he been away so long? Only an hour or two, by his reckoning, and he had left in the morning, and he had not felt any need to eat, and until a little while ago there had been even daylight; only now the darkness. 'Short days, short days!' he said to himself, slid off the sledge and went towards the inn.
paras.uz: — Sen, — deb birdan qichqirdi K. — ular allaqachon cherkov yaqinida edi, mehmonxonagacha yo'l uzoq emas edi, K. endi biror narsaga jur'at qilsa bo'lardi, — sen meni o'z mas'uliyating bilan olib yurishga jur'at qilayotganingdan juda hayronman, senga bunga ruxsat bormi? — Gerstekker bunga e'tibor bermadi va ot yonida xotirjam yurishda davom etdi. «Hey!» — qichqirdi K., chanadan biroz qor to'plab, uni Gerstekkerning qulog'iga to'g'ri urdi. Shunda u to'xtadi va o'girildi; lekin K. uni endi shunchalik yaqindan — chana biroz oldinga surilib ketgan edi — ko'rganida, bu bukchaygan, go'yo xo'rlangan qomatni, qandaydir bir-biridan farq qiladigan yonoqli — biri yassi, ikkinchisi botiq — qizil, charchagan, tor yuzni, ichida faqat bir nechta yakka-dukka tishlari bor ochiq, quloq solib turgan og'izni ko'rganida, avval g'araz bilan aytgan gapini endi achinib takrorlashga majbur bo'ldi: K.ni tashigani uchun Gerstekker jazolanmaydimi? «Nima istaysan?» — so'radi Gerstekker tushunmay, lekin boshqa izoh ham kutmadi, otga qichqirdi va ular yana yo'lga tushishdi. Mehmonxonaga deyarli yetib kelishganida — K. buni yo'l burilishidan tanidi — uning hayratiga, allaqachon butunlay qorong'i tushgan edi. Nahotki u shunchalik uzoq yo'qolgan bo'lsa? Uning hisobicha, faqat bir-ikki soat, u ertalab chiqib ketgan edi, ovqatga ehtiyoj ham sezmagan edi, yaqin paytgacha bir tekis kunduz yorug'i bor edi, faqat endi zulmat. «Qisqa kunlar, qisqa kunlar!» — dedi u o'ziga, chanadan sirpanib tushdi va mehmonxona tomon yurdi.

paras.en: Up on the little front steps of the house — very welcome to him — stood the landlord, holding up a lantern to light his way. Fleetingly remembering the carter, K. stopped; somewhere in the darkness someone was coughing — that was him. Well, he would see him again soon enough. Only when he was up beside the landlord, who greeted him humbly, did he notice a man on each side of the door. He took the lantern from the landlord's hand and shone it on the two; they were the men he had already met, who had been hailed as Artur and Jeremias. They saluted now. Remembering his army days, those happy times, he laughed. 'Who are you?' he asked, looking from one to the other. 'Your assistants,' they answered. 'They're the assistants,' the landlord confirmed quietly. 'What?' asked K. 'You are my old assistants, whom I told to follow me and whom I'm expecting?' They said yes. 'That's good,' said K. after a little while, 'it's good that you've come.' — 'By the way,' said K. after another little while, 'you're very late; you're very careless.' 'It was a long way,' said one of them. 'A long way,' K. repeated, 'but I met you coming from the Castle.' — 'Yes,' they said, without further explanation. 'Where are the instruments?' asked K. 'We haven't any,' they said. 'The instruments I entrusted to you,' said K. 'We haven't any,' they repeated. 'Oh, what fellows you are!' said K. 'Do you know anything about surveying?' — 'No,' they said. 'But if you are my old assistants, you must know about it,' said K., and pushed them ahead of him into the house.
paras.uz: Uyning kichkina old zinasi tepasida, uning uchun juda yoqimli tarzda, mehmonxona egasi turardi va fonusini ko'tarib, unga yo'l yoritib turardi. Aravakashni bir zum eslab, K. to'xtadi, qorong'ida qayerdadir kimdir yo'talardi — bu o'sha edi. Mayli, u uni tez orada yana ko'radi. Faqat mehmonxona egasining oldiga chiqqanidagina — u kamtarlik bilan salom berdi — eshikning ikki tomonida bittadan erkak turganini payqadi. U mehmonxona egasining qo'lidan fonusni olib, ikkovini yoritdi; bular u allaqachon uchratgan, Artur va Yeremiya deb chaqirilgan erkaklar edi. Ular endi harbiycha salom berishdi. Harbiy xizmat kunlarini, o'sha baxtli vaqtlarni eslab, u kuldi. «Kimsizlar?» — so'radi u birdan ikkinchisiga qarab. «Sizning yordamchilaringiz», deb javob berishdi ular. «Bular yordamchilar», tasdiqladi mehmonxona egasi sekin. «Nima? — so'radi K. — Sizlar men orqamdan kelishni buyurgan, men kutayotgan eski yordamchilarimmisizlar?» Ular «ha» deyishdi. «Bu yaxshi, — dedi K. biroz o'tgach, — kelganlaringiz yaxshi.» — «Aytgancha, — dedi K. yana biroz o'tgach, — sizlar juda kechikdingizlar, juda beparvosizlar.» «Yo'l uzoq edi», dedi ulardan biri. «Yo'l uzoq, — takrorladi K., — lekin men sizlarni Qasrdan kelayotganingizda uchratdim-ku.» — «Ha», deyishdi ular boshqa izohsiz. «Asboblar qayerda?» — so'radi K. «Bizda yo'q», deyishdi ular. «Men sizlarga ishonib topshirgan asboblar», dedi K. «Bizda yo'q», takrorlashdi ular. «Eh, sizlar ham odammisizlar! — dedi K. — Yer o'lchashdan biror narsa tushunasizlarmi?» — «Yo'q», deyishdi ular. «Lekin agar sizlar mening eski yordamchilarim bo'lsangiz, buni tushunishingiz kerak-ku», dedi K. va ularni o'zidan oldin uyga itarib kiritdi.

paras.en: Then the three of them sat rather silently in the taproom over their beer at a little table, K. in the middle, the assistants to his right and left. Otherwise only one table was occupied by peasants, much as on the evening before. 'You're a difficult pair,' said K., comparing their faces as he had done several times already. 'How am I supposed to tell you apart? You differ only in your names; otherwise you're as alike as —' he faltered, and then involuntarily went on — 'otherwise you're as alike as snakes.' They smiled. 'People usually tell us apart quite well,' they said in their defence. 'I believe it,' said K., 'I've seen it myself, but I see only with my own eyes, and with them I cannot tell you apart. So I shall treat you as a single man and call you both Artur — that's the name of one of you, isn't it? You, perhaps?' K. asked one of them. 'No,' said he, 'my name is Jeremias.' — 'It doesn't matter,' said K., 'I'll call you both Artur. If I send Artur somewhere, you both go; if I give Artur a job, you both do it. That has the great disadvantage for me that I can't use you for separate tasks, but the advantage that you will bear joint, undivided responsibility for everything I give you to do.
paras.uz: Keyin ular uchovlon umumiy zalda kichkina stolchada, ancha jim, pivo ustida o'tirishdi: K. o'rtada, yordamchilar o'ng va chap tomonida. Aks holda, xuddi kechagi oqshomdagidek, faqat bitta stolda dehqonlar o'tirardi. «Sizlar bilan qiyin, — dedi K. va avvalgidek ularning yuzlarini solishtirdi, — sizlarni qanday ajrataman? Sizlar faqat ismlaringiz bilan farq qilasizlar, aks holda bir-biringizga xuddi… — u tutilib qoldi, keyin beixtiyor davom etdi, — aks holda bir-biringizga xuddi ilonlardek o'xshaysizlar.» Ular jilmayishdi. «Odatda bizni yaxshi ajratishadi», deyishdi ular o'zlarini oqlab. «Ishonaman, — dedi K., — men o'zim bunga guvoh bo'ldim, lekin men faqat o'z ko'zim bilan ko'raman, ular bilan esa sizlarni ajrata olmayman. Shuning uchun sizlarga bitta odamdek munosabatda bo'laman va ikkalangizni ham Artur deb atayman — axir biringizning ismi shunday-ku. Balki sendir?» — so'radi K. ulardan biridan. «Yo'q, — dedi u, — mening ismim Yeremiya.» — «Farqi yo'q, — dedi K., — ikkalangizni ham Artur deb atayman. Agar Arturni biror joyga yuborsam, ikkalangiz ham borasizlar, agar Arturga biror ish bersam, ikkalangiz ham qilasizlar; buning men uchun katta kamchiligi shundaki, sizlardan alohida ishlar uchun foydalana olmayman, lekin afzalligi shundaki, men topshirgan hamma narsa uchun birgalikda, bo'linmagan holda javob berasizlar.

paras.en: How you share out the work between yourselves is all the same to me; only you mustn't make excuses by blaming each other. For me you are a single man.' They thought this over and said: 'That would be very unpleasant for us.' — 'How could it not be?' said K. 'Of course it must be unpleasant for you, but that's how it stays.' For a little while now K. had watched one of the peasants creeping round the table; at last he made up his mind, went up to one of the assistants and wanted to whisper something to him. 'Excuse me,' said K., struck the table with his hand and stood up, 'these are my assistants, and we are having a meeting. Nobody has the right to disturb us.' — 'Oh, sorry, sorry,' said the peasant anxiously and backed away to his own company. 'This above all you must observe,' said K., sitting down again. 'You may not speak to anyone without my permission. I am a stranger here, and if you are my old assistants, you are strangers too. We three strangers must therefore stick together; give me your hands on it.' All too eagerly they held them out to K. 'Keep your paws,' he said, 'but my order stands. I'm going to bed now, and I advise you to do the same. Today we have lost a working day; tomorrow work must begin very early. You must get hold of a sledge for the drive to the Castle and be ready with it here in front of the house at six o'clock.' — 'All right,' said one of them.
paras.uz: Ishni o'zaro qanday bo'lishasizlar — menga farqi yo'q, faqat bir-biringizni aybdor qilib bahona qilmasligingiz kerak, men uchun sizlar bitta odamsizlar.» Ular buni o'ylab ko'rishdi va dedilar: «Bu biz uchun juda noxush bo'lardi.» — «Qanday bo'lmasin, — dedi K., — albatta, bu sizlar uchun noxush bo'lishi kerak, lekin shunday qoladi.» K. allaqachon bir muddatdan beri dehqonlardan biri stol atrofida aylanib yurganini ko'rib turardi; nihoyat u jur'at qilib, yordamchilardan biriga yaqinlashdi va unga nimadir pichirlamoqchi bo'ldi. «Kechirasiz, — dedi K., qo'li bilan stolni urib, o'rnidan turdi, — bular mening yordamchilarim va biz hozir kengash o'tkazyapmiz. Hech kim bizni bezovta qilishga haqli emas.» — «Oh, kechirasiz, kechirasiz», dedi dehqon qo'rqib va orqasi bilan o'z davrasiga qaytdi. «Mana shunga avvalo rioya qilishingiz kerak, — dedi K. yana o'tirib. — Mening ruxsatimsiz hech kim bilan gaplasha olmaysizlar. Men bu yerda begonaman va agar sizlar mening eski yordamchilarim bo'lsangiz, sizlar ham begonasizlar. Shuning uchun biz uch begona bir-birimizni qo'llab-quvvatlashimiz kerak, shunga qo'llaringizni beringlar.» Ular haddan tashqari tayyorlik bilan qo'llarini K.ga cho'zishdi. «Panjalaringizni o'zingizga qoldiringlar, — dedi u, — lekin buyrug'im kuchda. Men hozir uxlashga ketaman, sizlarga ham shuni maslahat beraman. Bugun bir ish kunini boy berdik, ertaga ish juda erta boshlanishi kerak. Qasrga borish uchun chana topib, soat oltida u bilan shu yerda, uy oldida tayyor turishingiz kerak.» — «Yaxshi», dedi ulardan biri.

paras.en: But the other broke in: 'You say all right, and yet you know it's impossible.' — 'Quiet,' said K. 'I suppose you want to start being different from each other.' But now the first one too said: 'He's right, it's impossible; no stranger may go into the Castle without permission.' — 'Where does one have to apply for permission?' — 'I don't know, perhaps to the steward.' 'Then we'll apply by telephone. Telephone the steward at once, both of you!' They ran to the apparatus and got the connection — how they jostled each other there! In outward things they were ridiculously obedient — and asked whether K. might come to the Castle with them tomorrow. The 'No!' of the answer could be heard by K. at his table. But the answer was more detailed still; it ran: 'Neither tomorrow nor any other time.' — 'I'll telephone myself,' said K., and stood up. While K. and his assistants had so far attracted little attention, apart from the incident with the one peasant, his last remark aroused general interest. Everyone stood up with K., and although the landlord tried to push them back, they grouped themselves around him at the telephone in a tight semicircle. The prevailing opinion among them was that K. would get no answer at all. K. had to ask them to be quiet; he did not ask to hear their opinions.
paras.uz: Ikkinchisi esa gapga aralashdi: «Sen «yaxshi» deyapsan, lekin bu mumkin emasligini bilasan-ku.» — «Jim, — dedi K., — bir-biringizdan farq qila boshlamoqchimisizlar?» Lekin endi birinchisi ham dedi: «U haq, bu mumkin emas, ruxsatsiz hech bir begona Qasrga kira olmaydi.» — «Ruxsat uchun qayerga murojaat qilish kerak?» — «Bilmayman, balki kastelyanga.» «Unda telefon orqali murojaat qilamiz, darhol kastelyanga telefon qilinglar, ikkalangiz ham!» Ular apparatga yugurishdi, ulanishga erishishdi — ular u yerda qanday turtinishdi! Tashqi narsalarda ular kulgili darajada itoatkor edilar — va K. ertaga ular bilan Qasrga kelishi mumkinmi, deb so'rashdi. Javobdagi «Yo'q!»ni K. o'z stolidan eshitdi. Lekin javob bundan ham batafsilroq edi, u shunday edi: «Na ertaga, na boshqa vaqt.» — «O'zim telefon qilaman», dedi K. va o'rnidan turdi. K. va uning yordamchilariga hozirgacha, bitta dehqon bilan bo'lgan voqeani hisobga olmaganda, kam e'tibor berilgan bo'lsa, uning so'nggi gapi umumiy diqqatni tortdi. Hamma K. bilan birga o'rnidan turdi va mehmonxona egasi ularni orqaga surishga urinsa ham, ular apparat yonida uning atrofida zich yarim doira bo'lib to'planishdi. Ular orasida K. umuman javob olmaydi, degan fikr ustun edi. K. ulardan jim turishni so'rashga majbur bo'ldi — u ularning fikrlarini eshitishni talab qilmayotgan edi.

paras.en: From the earpiece came a humming such as K. had never heard before when telephoning. It was as if, out of the humming of countless children's voices — but this humming was not a humming either, it was the singing of the most distant, the very most distant voices — as if out of this humming, in a quite impossible way, there formed a single high but strong voice that beat against the ear as though demanding to penetrate deeper than merely into one's wretched hearing. K. listened without telephoning; he had propped his left arm on the telephone stand and listened like that.
paras.uz: Go'shakdan K. telefon qilganda ilgari hech qachon eshitmagan g'uvullash chiqdi. Go'yo son-sanoqsiz bolalar ovozlarining g'uvullashidan — lekin bu g'uvullash ham g'uvullash emas, balki eng uzoq, eng-eng uzoq ovozlarning qo'shig'i edi — go'yo shu g'uvullashdan mutlaqo imkonsiz bir tarzda yagona baland, lekin kuchli ovoz shakllanib, quloqqa urilayotgandek, go'yo faqat bechora eshitish qobiliyatidan chuqurroq kirib borishni talab qilayotgandek edi. K. telefonda gapirmasdan tinglardi; chap qo'lini telefon tokchasiga tirab, shunday tinglardi.

paras.en: He did not know for how long; until the landlord plucked at his coat — a messenger had come for him. 'Go away!' K. shouted, losing control, and perhaps into the telephone, for now someone answered. The following conversation developed: 'Oswald here, who's there?' came a stern, haughty voice, with a slight speech defect, it seemed to K., which it tried to make up for with an extra dose of sternness. K. hesitated to give his name; in front of the telephone he was defenceless; the other man could thunder at him, put down the receiver, and K. would have blocked a path that was perhaps not unimportant. K.'s hesitation made the man impatient. 'Who's there?' he repeated, and added: 'I should be very glad if there were not so much telephoning from your end; there was a call only a moment ago.' K. ignored this remark and announced, with a sudden decision: 'This is the land surveyor's assistant.' 'Which assistant? Which gentleman? Which land surveyor?' K. remembered yesterday's telephone conversation. 'Ask Fritz,' he said curtly. To his own astonishment it worked. But even more than at its working, he marvelled at the uniformity of the service there. The answer was: 'I know already. The eternal land surveyor. Yes, yes. What else? Which assistant?' 'Josef,' said K. The muttering of the peasants behind his back disturbed him a little; evidently they did not approve of his not giving his proper name.
paras.uz: U qancha vaqt ekanini bilmasdi; mehmonxona egasi uning kamzulidan tortib, unga xabarchi kelganini aytguncha. «Yo'qol!» — deb qichqirdi K. o'zini tutolmay, balki telefonga ham, chunki endi kimdir javob berdi. Quyidagi suhbat bo'lib o'tdi: «Bu yerda Osvald, u yerda kim?» — degan qattiq, mag'rur ovoz yangradi; K.ga tuyulishicha, unda kichik bir nutq nuqsoni bor edi va u buni qo'shimcha qattiqlik bilan qoplashga urinardi. K. ismini aytishga ikkilandi; telefon oldida u himoyasiz edi, narigi odam uni ezib tashlashi, go'shakni qo'yib qo'yishi mumkin edi va K. balki muhim bo'lgan bir yo'lni o'ziga yopib qo'ygan bo'lardi. K.ning ikkilanishi erkakni toqatsiz qildi. «U yerda kim?» — takrorladi u va qo'shib qo'ydi: «Sizning tomondan shunchalik ko'p telefon qilinmasa, juda xursand bo'lardim, bir lahza oldin ham telefon qilindi.» K. bu gapga e'tibor bermadi va birdan qaror qilib bildirdi: «Bu yerda janob yer o'lchovchining yordamchisi.» «Qaysi yordamchi? Qaysi janob? Qaysi yer o'lchovchi?» K.ning esiga kechagi telefon suhbati tushdi. «Fritsdan so'rang», dedi u qisqagina. Bu o'zining ham hayratiga yordam berdi. Lekin yordam berganidan ko'ra ham u yerdagi xizmatning bir xilligidan ko'proq hayron bo'ldi. Javob shunday bo'ldi: «Bilaman. Abadiy yer o'lchovchi. Ha, ha. Yana nima? Qaysi yordamchi?» «Yozef», dedi K. Orqasidagi dehqonlarning g'o'ldirashi uni biroz bezovta qildi; aftidan, ular uning o'zini to'g'ri tanishtirmaganini ma'qullamayotgan edilar.

paras.en: But K. had no time to bother with them, for the conversation absorbed him greatly. 'Josef?' came the question back. 'The assistants are called' — a short pause; evidently he was asking someone else for the names — 'Artur and Jeremias.' 'Those are the new assistants,' said K. 'No, those are the old ones.' — 'They are the new ones; I am the old one, who followed the land surveyor here today.' — 'No!' came a shout now. 'Then who am I?' asked K., as calm as before. And after a pause the same voice, with the same speech defect, and yet like another, deeper, more respectable voice, said: 'You are the old assistant.'
paras.uz: Lekin K.da ular bilan shug'ullanishga vaqt yo'q edi, chunki suhbat uni butunlay band qilgan edi. «Yozefmi? — deb qayta so'radi ovoz. — Yordamchilarning ismi… — kichik pauza, aftidan, u ismlarni boshqa birovdan so'rayotgan edi, — Artur va Yeremiya.» «Bular yangi yordamchilar», dedi K. «Yo'q, bular eskilari.» — «Bular yangilari, men esa eskisiman, bugun janob yer o'lchovchining orqasidan kelganman.» — «Yo'q!» — deb qichqirdi endi ovoz. «Unda men kimman?» — so'radi K. avvalgidek xotirjam. Va pauzadan keyin o'sha ovoz, o'sha nutq nuqsoni bilan, lekin go'yo boshqa, chuqurroq, hurmatliroq ovozdek dedi: «Sen eski yordamchisan.»

paras.en: K. listened to the sound of the voice and nearly missed the question: 'What do you want?' He would have liked best to put down the receiver already. He expected nothing more from this conversation. Only under compulsion did he quickly ask: 'When may my master come to the Castle?' — 'Never,' was the answer. 'Good,' said K., and hung up the receiver.
paras.uz: K. ovozning jarangiga quloq solib, savolni deyarli eshitmay qoldi: «Nima istaysan?» U go'shakni allaqachon qo'yib qo'yishni eng ko'p istardi. Bu suhbatdan endi hech narsa kutmasdi. Faqat majburan tezda so'radi: «Xo'jayinim Qasrga qachon kelishi mumkin?» — «Hech qachon», degan javob bo'ldi. «Yaxshi», dedi K. va go'shakni ilib qo'ydi.

paras.en: The peasants behind him had already moved right up close to him. The assistants, with many sidelong glances at him, were busy keeping the peasants away from him. But it seemed to be only a comedy, and besides, the peasants, satisfied with the outcome of the conversation, were slowly giving way. Then their group was parted from behind by a man coming quickly through, who bowed to K. and handed him a letter. K. kept the letter in his hand and looked at the man, who seemed to him for the moment more important. There was a great resemblance between him and the assistants: he was as slim as they were, just as tightly dressed, just as supple and nimble — and yet quite different. If only K. had had him as an assistant instead! He reminded him a little of the woman with the baby he had seen at the master tanner's. He was dressed almost in white; the clothes were probably not of silk, they were winter clothes like all the others, but they had the delicacy and solemnity of silk. His face was bright and open, his eyes very large. His smile was extraordinarily encouraging; he passed his hand over his face as though to chase the smile away, but he did not manage it. 'Who are you?' asked K. 'My name is Barnabas,' he said. 'I am a messenger.' His lips opened and closed manfully and yet gently as he spoke.
paras.uz: Orqasidagi dehqonlar allaqachon unga juda yaqin kelib qolishgan edi. Yordamchilar unga ko'p yonlama qarab, dehqonlarni undan uzoqda ushlab turish bilan band edilar. Lekin bu faqat komediyadek tuyulardi, buning ustiga dehqonlar suhbat natijasidan mamnun bo'lib, asta-sekin chekinishardi. Shunda ularning to'dasini orqadan tez qadam bilan bir erkak yorib o'tdi, K.ga ta'zim qilib, unga maktub uzatdi. K. maktubni qo'lida ushlab turib, hozircha unga muhimroq tuyulgan erkakka qaradi. U bilan yordamchilar o'rtasida katta o'xshashlik bor edi: u ham ular kabi xipcha, xuddi shunday tor kiyingan, xuddi ular kabi epchil va chaqqon edi, lekin baribir butunlay boshqacha. Qaniydi K.ning yordamchisi u bo'lsa! U K.ga ko'nchi ustanikida ko'rgan go'dakli ayolni biroz eslatdi. U deyarli oq kiyingan edi, kiyimi ipakdan bo'lmasa kerak, boshqalarniki kabi qishki kiyim edi, lekin unda ipak libosning nozikligi va tantanavorligi bor edi. Yuzi yorug' va ochiq, ko'zlari g'oyat katta edi. Jilmayishi g'ayrioddiy darajada dalda beruvchi edi; u go'yo bu jilmayishni haydamoqchidek qo'lini yuziga yurgizdi, lekin uddalay olmadi. «Sen kimsan?» — so'radi K. «Mening ismim Barnabas, — dedi u. — Men xabarchiman.» Gapirganda lablari erkakcha, lekin muloyim ochilib-yopilardi.

paras.en: 'Do you like it here?' asked K., and pointed to the peasants, in whom he had still not lost interest — with their faces downright tormented, as though their skulls had been beaten flat on top and their features had formed in the pain of the beating, with their thick lips and open mouths, watching him and yet also not watching, for sometimes their eyes wandered off and stuck to some indifferent object before returning. And K. pointed to the assistants too, who were holding each other round the waist, leaning cheek to cheek and smiling — whether humbly or mockingly, one could not tell. He pointed out all of them as if he were introducing an escort forced on him by special circumstances, and expected — there was an intimacy in this, and that was what mattered to K. — that Barnabas would always distinguish between him and them. But Barnabas — in all innocence, it was plain to see — did not take up the question at all; he let it pass over him, as a well-trained servant lets pass a remark of his master's that is only apparently meant for him; he merely looked about in the sense of the question, waved a greeting to acquaintances among the peasants, and exchanged a few words with the assistants, all freely and independently, without mixing with them. Rebuffed but not ashamed, K. turned back to the letter in his hand and opened it. It read: 'Dear Sir,
paras.uz: «Bu yer senga yoqadimi?» — so'radi K. va hamon qiziqishini yo'qotmagan dehqonlarni ko'rsatdi: ularning yuzlari rosa azoblangan edi — bosh suyagi go'yo tepadan urib yassilangandek, yuz chiziqlari esa urilish og'rig'ida shakllangandek edi — qalin lablari, ochiq og'izlari bilan ular qarab turishardi, lekin baribir qaramas ham edilar, chunki ba'zan nigohlari chetga ketib, qaytishdan oldin qandaydir befarq buyumga yopishib qolardi. Keyin K. bir-birini quchoqlab, yuzma-yuz suyanib, jilmayib turgan yordamchilarni ham ko'rsatdi — kamtarona yoki masxaraomuz ekanini bilib bo'lmasdi; u bularning hammasini go'yo unga alohida vaziyatlar tufayli majburan tirkalgan mulozimlarni tanishtirayotgandek ko'rsatdi va kutdiki — bunda samimiylik bor edi, K. uchun aynan shu muhim edi — Barnabas doim u bilan ular o'rtasida farq qiladi. Lekin Barnabas — albatta, butun soddaligi bilan, buni ko'rish mumkin edi — savolni umuman qabul qilmadi, go'yo yaxshi tarbiyalangan xizmatkor xo'jayinning faqat zohiran unga qaratilgan so'zini o'tkazib yuborgandek o'tkazib yubordi, faqat savol ma'nosida atrofga qaradi, dehqonlar orasidagi tanishlariga qo'l silkitib salom berdi va yordamchilar bilan bir-ikki so'z almashdi — bularning hammasi erkin va mustaqil, ular bilan aralashib ketmasdan. Rad etilgan, lekin uyalmagan K. qo'lidagi maktubga qaytdi va uni ochdi. Uning matni shunday edi: «Hurmatli janob!

paras.en: You have, as you know, been taken into the Count's service. Your immediate superior is the mayor of the village, who will also tell you everything further about your work and the terms of your pay, and to whom you will also be accountable. Nevertheless I too shall not lose sight of you. Barnabas, the bearer of this letter, will call on you from time to time to learn your wishes and report them to me. You will always find me ready to oblige you as far as possible. It matters to me to have contented workers.' The signature was illegible, but printed beside it was: Head of Department X. 'Wait!' K. said to Barnabas, who was bowing, and then called the landlord to show him a room; he wanted to be alone with the letter for a while. At the same time he remembered that Barnabas, for all the liking he felt for him, was after all only a messenger, and had him given some beer. He watched how he would take it; evidently he took it very gladly and drank at once. Then K. went with the landlord. In the little house they had been able to get ready nothing for K. but a small attic room, and even that had caused difficulties, for two maids who had slept there until now had had to be put up somewhere else.
paras.uz: Siz, o'zingiz bilganingizdek, graflik xizmatiga qabul qilindingiz. Sizning bevosita boshlig'ingiz — qishloq oqsoqoli, u sizga ishingiz va maosh shartlari haqida batafsil ma'lumot beradi va siz unga hisob berishingiz kerak bo'ladi. Shunga qaramay, men ham sizni ko'zdan qochirmayman. Ushbu maktubni yetkazgan Barnabas vaqti-vaqti bilan sizdan istaklaringizni bilib, menga yetkazish uchun xabar olib turadi. Meni doim imkon qadar sizga yordam berishga tayyor topasiz. Mamnun ishchilarga ega bo'lish men uchun muhim.» Imzo o'qib bo'lmasdi, lekin uning yoniga bosilgan edi: X idorasi boshlig'i. «Kut!» — dedi K. ta'zim qilayotgan Barnabasga, keyin mehmonxona egasini chaqirib, unga xona ko'rsatishni so'radi: u maktub bilan bir muddat yolg'iz qolmoqchi edi. Shu bilan birga u Barnabasga bo'lgan butun mehriga qaramay, u baribir faqat xabarchi ekanini esladi va unga pivo berishni buyurdi. U uni qanday qabul qilishini kuzatdi; u, aftidan, juda bajonidil qabul qildi va darhol ichdi. Keyin K. mehmonxona egasi bilan ketdi. Uychada K. uchun kichkina chordoq xonasidan boshqa hech narsa tayyorlay olishmagan edi, hatto bu ham qiyinchilik tug'dirgan edi, chunki hozirgacha u yerda uxlagan ikki xizmatkor qizni boshqa joyga joylashtirish kerak bo'lgan edi.

paras.en: In fact they had done nothing except move the maids out; the room was otherwise unchanged, no sheets on the only bed, just a couple of pillows and a horse blanket, in the state in which everything had been left after the previous night. On the wall a few holy pictures and photographs of soldiers. It had not even been aired; evidently they hoped the new guest would not stay long and did nothing to keep him. But K. accepted everything, wrapped himself in the blanket, sat down at the table and by the light of a candle began to read the letter again.
paras.uz: Aslida qizlarni chiqarib yuborishdan boshqa hech narsa qilinmagan edi, xona boshqa jihatdan o'zgarmagan bo'lsa kerak: yagona karavotda choyshab yo'q, faqat bir-ikki yostiq va ot yopinchig'i, hammasi o'tgan kechadan qanday qolgan bo'lsa, shunday holatda. Devorda bir nechta avliyolar suratlari va askarlarning fotosuratlari. Hatto shamollatilmagan ham edi; aftidan, yangi mehmon uzoq qolmaydi, deb umid qilishar va uni ushlab qolish uchun hech narsa qilishmasdi. Lekin K. hamma narsaga rozi edi, yopinchiqqa o'ralib, stolga o'tirdi va sham yorug'ida maktubni yana o'qiy boshladi.

paras.en: It was not consistent. There were passages where he was spoken to as a free man whose own will was acknowledged — so it was with the form of address, so with the passage about his wishes. But again there were passages where he was treated, openly or covertly, as a minor worker hardly noticeable from that head of department's seat: the head had to make an effort 'not to lose sight of him'; his superior was only the village mayor, to whom he was even accountable; his only colleague was perhaps the village policeman. These were undoubtedly contradictions, and they were so visible that they must have been intended. The idea — mad, in the face of such an authority — that indecision had played a part here barely crossed K.'s mind. Rather, he saw in it a choice openly offered him: it was left to him what he wanted to make of the letter's instructions — whether he wanted to be a village worker with a distinguishing but merely apparent connection to the Castle, or an apparent village worker who in reality let his whole working relationship be determined by the messages of Barnabas. K. did not hesitate to choose, and would not have hesitated even without the experiences he had already had.
paras.uz: U bir xil emas edi. Ba'zi joylarda u bilan o'z irodasi tan olingan erkin odam bilan gaplashgandek gaplashilgan edi — murojaat shakli ham, uning istaklariga oid joy ham shunday edi. Lekin yana shunday joylar bor ediki, unda unga ochiq yoki yashirin tarzda o'sha boshliqning o'rindig'idan deyarli ko'rinmaydigan kichik bir ishchi sifatida munosabatda bo'lingan edi: boshliq uni «ko'zdan qochirmaslik» uchun harakat qilishi kerak edi, uning boshlig'i faqat qishloq oqsoqoli bo'lib, unga hatto hisob berishi kerak edi, uning yagona hamkasbi, ehtimol, qishloq politsiyachisi edi. Bular shubhasiz qarama-qarshiliklar edi, ular shunchalik ko'zga tashlanardiki, ataylab qilingan bo'lishi kerak edi. Bunday idoraga nisbatan telbalarcha bo'lgan — bu yerda ikkilanish rol o'ynagan, degan — fikr K.ning xayolidan zo'rg'a o'tdi. Aksincha, u bunda unga ochiq taklif qilingan tanlovni ko'rdi: maktub ko'rsatmalaridan nima yasashini o'zi hal qilishi kerak edi — u Qasr bilan baribir ajralib turadigan, lekin faqat zohiriy aloqaga ega qishloq ishchisi bo'lishni istaydimi, yoki zohiran qishloq ishchisi bo'lib, aslida butun mehnat munosabatini Barnabasning xabarlari belgilashiga yo'l qo'yadimi. K. tanlashda ikkilanmadi, hatto allaqachon orttirgan tajribalarisiz ham ikkilanmagan bo'lardi.

paras.en: Only as a village worker, removed as far as possible from the gentlemen of the Castle, could he achieve anything at the Castle. These people in the village, still so mistrustful of him, would begin to talk once he had become, if not their friend, at least their fellow villager; and once he was indistinguishable from Gerstäcker or Lasemann — and that must happen very quickly, everything depended on it — then surely all the paths would open to him at one stroke, paths that, had it depended only on the gentlemen above and their favour, would have stayed for ever not merely closed to him but invisible. There was a danger, of course, and the letter stressed it enough; it presented it with a certain relish, as though it were inescapable. It was being a worker. Service, superior, work, terms of pay, accountability, worker — the letter swarmed with them, and even when something else, something more personal, was said, it was said from that point of view. If K. wanted to become a worker he could, but then in all dreadful seriousness, without any prospect of anything else. K. knew he was not threatened with real compulsion; he did not fear that, and here least of all. But the power of discouraging surroundings, of growing used to disappointments, the power of the imperceptible influences of every moment — those he did fear; yet with this danger he had to risk the fight.
paras.uz: Faqat qishloq ishchisi sifatida, Qasr janoblaridan imkon qadar uzoqlashgan holda u Qasrda biror narsaga erisha olardi; hali unga shunchalik ishonchsiz bo'lgan qishloqdagi bu odamlar u ularning do'sti bo'lmasa ham, hech bo'lmaganda qishloqdoshi bo'lganida gapira boshlashardi; va bir marta u Gerstekker yoki Lazemandan ajratib bo'lmaydigan bo'lsa — bu juda tez sodir bo'lishi kerak edi, hamma narsa shunga bog'liq edi — unda, albatta, unga birdaniga barcha yo'llar ochilardi; agar hamma narsa faqat tepadagi janoblar va ularning marhamatiga bog'liq bo'lganida, bu yo'llar unga abadiy nafaqat yopiq, balki ko'rinmas bo'lib qolgan bo'lardi. Albatta, bir xavf bor edi va maktubda u yetarlicha ta'kidlangan, go'yo undan qochib bo'lmaydigandek, qandaydir mamnuniyat bilan tasvirlangan edi. Bu — ishchi bo'lish edi. Xizmat, boshliq, ish, maosh shartlari, hisob berish, ishchi — maktub bular bilan to'lib-toshgan edi, hatto boshqa, shaxsiyroq narsa aytilganda ham, u o'sha nuqtai nazardan aytilgan edi. Agar K. ishchi bo'lishni istasa, bo'la olardi, lekin unda butun dahshatli jiddiylik bilan, boshqa hech qanday istiqbolsiz. K. haqiqiy majburlash bilan tahdid qilinmayotganini bilardi, undan qo'rqmasdi, ayniqsa bu yerda; lekin tushkunlikka soluvchi muhitning kuchi, ko'ngil qolishlarga ko'nikishning kuchi, har lahzaning sezilmas ta'sirlarining kuchi — mana bulardan u, albatta, qo'rqardi, lekin bu xavf bilan kurashga jur'at qilishi kerak edi.

paras.en: Nor did the letter conceal that, if it came to fighting, K. had had the boldness to begin it. It was said subtly, and only an uneasy conscience — uneasy, not bad — could notice it: it was the three words 'as you know' regarding his being taken into service. K. had reported, and since then he knew, as the letter put it, that he had been taken on. K. took a picture off the wall and hung the letter on the nail. He would live in this room; here the letter should hang.
paras.uz: Maktub, agar kurash bo'ladigan bo'lsa, uni boshlashga K. jasorat qilganini ham yashirmagan edi; bu nozik aytilgan edi va faqat bezovta vijdon — bezovta, yomon emas — uni payqashi mumkin edi: bu uning xizmatga qabul qilinishiga oid «o'zingiz bilganingizdek» degan uch so'z edi. K. o'zini taklif qilgan edi va shundan beri, maktub ifodalaganidek, qabul qilinganini bilardi. K. devordan bir suratni olib, maktubni mixga ildi; u shu xonada yashaydi, maktub shu yerda osilib turishi kerak.

paras.en: Then he went down to the taproom. Barnabas was sitting with the assistants at a small table. 'Ah, there you are,' said K. for no reason, only because he was glad to see Barnabas. He jumped up at once. K. had hardly come in when the peasants rose to approach him; it had already become their habit always to run after him. 'What do you keep wanting from me?' cried K. They did not take it amiss and slowly turned back to their places. One of them, by way of explanation as he went, said lightly, with an inscrutable smile that some of the others took up: 'One always hears something new,' and he licked his lips as though the new thing were food. K. said nothing conciliatory; it was good if they got a little respect for him. But he had hardly sat down beside Barnabas when he felt a peasant's breath on his neck; he had come, he said, to fetch the salt cellar, but K. stamped his foot in annoyance, and the peasant ran off without the salt cellar. It was really easy to get at K.; one had only, for instance, to set the peasants on him. Their stubborn interest seemed to him worse than the reserve of the others, and besides, it was reserve too, for had K. sat down at their table, they would certainly not have stayed sitting there. Only the presence of Barnabas kept him from making a scene. But he did turn round threateningly to them once more, and they too were turned towards him.
paras.uz: Keyin u umumiy zalga tushdi. Barnabas yordamchilar bilan kichkina stol yonida o'tirardi. «Ha, shu yerdamisan», dedi K. hech sababsiz, faqat Barnabasni ko'rganidan xursand bo'lgani uchun. U darhol sakrab turdi. K. kirishi bilanoq dehqonlar unga yaqinlashish uchun o'rnidan turishdi; doim uning ortidan yugurish allaqachon ularning odatiga aylangan edi. «Mendan doim nima istaysizlar?» — qichqirdi K. Ular xafa bo'lishmadi va asta-sekin o'z joylariga qaytishdi. Ulardan biri ketayotib izoh tariqasida, yengil, boshqa ba'zilar ham ilib olgan tushunib bo'lmas jilmayish bilan dedi: «Doim biror yangilik eshitiladi», va go'yo yangilik taomdek lablarini yaladi. K. hech qanday yarashuvchi gap aytmadi; agar ular unga biroz hurmat ko'rsatsa, yaxshi edi. Lekin u Barnabasning yoniga o'tirishi bilanoq ensasida bir dehqonning nafasini his qildi; u, aytishicha, tuzdonni olgani kelgan edi, lekin K. jahl bilan oyog'ini depsindi va dehqon tuzdonsiz qochib ketdi. K.ga yetib olish haqiqatan ham oson edi, masalan, dehqonlarni unga qarshi gij-gijlash kifoya edi; ularning qaysar qiziqishi unga boshqalarning yopiqligidan ham yomonroq tuyulardi, buning ustiga bu ham yopiqlik edi, chunki agar K. ularning stoliga o'tirsa, ular, albatta, u yerda o'tirib qolishmasdi. Faqat Barnabasning borligi uni janjal ko'tarishdan to'xtatib turdi. Lekin u baribir yana bir bor ularga tahdidli o'girildi, ular ham unga qarab turishardi.

paras.en: But when he saw them sitting there like that, each in his place, without talking to one another, without any visible connection between them, connected only by all staring at him, it seemed to him that it was not malice at all that made them pursue him; perhaps they really wanted something from him and just could not say it; and if not that, then perhaps it was only childishness, which seemed to be at home here. Was not the landlord childish too, holding with both hands a glass of beer that he was supposed to take to some guest, standing still, looking at K., and not hearing a call from the landlady, who had leaned out of the little kitchen hatch?
paras.uz: Lekin ularning shunday o'tirganini — har biri o'z joyida, bir-biri bilan gaplashmasdan, o'zaro ko'rinadigan aloqasiz, faqat hammasi unga tikilib turishi bilan bog'langan holda — ko'rganida, unga ularni uning ortidan quvishga majbur qilayotgan narsa umuman g'araz emasdek tuyuldi; balki ular haqiqatan ham undan nimadir istashar-u, faqat aytolmasdilar; agar bunday bo'lmasa, balki bu faqat bu yerda uyidagidek bo'lgan bolalikdir; biror mehmonga olib borishi kerak bo'lgan bir stakan pivoni ikki qo'llab ushlab, to'xtab, K.ga qarab turgan va oshxona tuynugidan engashgan bekaning chaqiruvini eshitmagan mehmonxona egasi ham bolalarcha emasmidi?

paras.en: More calmly K. turned to Barnabas. He would have liked to get rid of the assistants but could find no pretext; anyway, they were gazing quietly into their beer. 'I have read the letter,' K. began. 'Do you know what's in it?' — 'No,' said Barnabas; his look seemed to say more than his words. Perhaps K. was deceiving himself here for the good, as with the peasants for the bad; but the comfort of his presence remained. 'You are mentioned in the letter too; you are to carry messages now and then between me and the head of department, and so I thought you knew what was in it.' — 'I was only told,' said Barnabas, 'to deliver the letter, wait until it had been read, and, if you think it necessary, bring back an answer, by word of mouth or in writing.' — 'Good,' said K., 'no writing is needed. Tell the head of department — what is his name? I couldn't read the signature.' 'Klamm,' said Barnabas. 'Then give Herr Klamm my thanks for taking me on, and also for his special kindness, which I, as one who has not yet proved himself here at all, know how to value. I shall act entirely in accordance with his intentions. I have no special wishes today.' Barnabas, who had listened closely, asked to be allowed to repeat the message in front of K. K. allowed it, and Barnabas repeated everything word for word. Then he stood up to take his leave.
paras.uz: Xotirjamroq bo'lib K. Barnabasga murojaat qildi; yordamchilarni ketkazishni istardi, lekin bahona topa olmadi. Aytgancha, ular jimgina pivolariga qarab o'tirishardi. «Maktubni, — deb boshladi K., — o'qidim. Mazmunini bilasanmi?» — «Yo'q», dedi Barnabas, uning nigohi so'zlaridan ko'proq narsa aytayotgandek edi. Balki K. bu yerda yaxshilik tomoniga adashayotgandir, xuddi dehqonlarda yomonlik tomoniga adashganidek; lekin uning borligining yoqimliligi qolaverdi. «Maktubda sen haqingda ham gap bor: sen vaqti-vaqti bilan men bilan boshliq o'rtasida xabar yetkazishing kerak ekan, shuning uchun mazmunini bilasan, deb o'ylagan edim.» — «Menga faqat, — dedi Barnabas, — maktubni topshirish, u o'qilguncha kutish va, agar zarur deb bilsang, og'zaki yoki yozma javobni olib qaytish topshirilgan.» — «Yaxshi, — dedi K., — yozishga hojat yo'q, janob boshliqqa yetkaz — aytgancha, uning ismi nima? Imzoni o'qiy olmadim.» «Klamm», dedi Barnabas. «Unda janob Klammga meni qabul qilgani uchun, shuningdek, bu yerda hali o'zini umuman ko'rsatmagan odam sifatida qadrlay oladigan alohida iltifoti uchun minnatdorchiligimni yetkaz. Men butunlay uning niyatlariga muvofiq harakat qilaman. Bugun alohida istaklarim yo'q.» Diqqat bilan tinglagan Barnabas topshiriqni K.ning oldida takrorlashga ruxsat so'radi. K. ruxsat berdi, Barnabas hammasini so'zma-so'z takrorladi. Keyin xayrlashish uchun o'rnidan turdi.

paras.en: All the while K. had been studying his face; now he did so for the last time. Barnabas was about as tall as K., yet his gaze seemed to bend down to K. — but almost humbly; it was impossible that this man could put anyone to shame. Of course he was only a messenger and did not know the contents of the letters he had to deliver, but his look too, his smile, his walk, seemed to be a message, even if he knew nothing of it. And K. held out his hand to him, which evidently surprised him, for he had meant only to bow.
paras.uz: Butun vaqt davomida K. uning yuzini sinchiklab kuzatgan edi, endi buni oxirgi marta qildi. Barnabas taxminan K. bo'yida edi, shunga qaramay uning nigohi K.ga pastga qaratilgandek tuyulardi, lekin bu deyarli kamtarlik bilan sodir bo'lardi; bu odam kimnidir uyaltirishi mumkin emas edi. Albatta, u faqat xabarchi edi, olib borishi kerak bo'lgan maktublarning mazmunini bilmasdi, lekin uning nigohi, jilmayishi, yurishi ham — u bundan hech narsa bilmasa ham — bir xabar bo'lib tuyulardi. Va K. unga qo'l uzatdi, bu, aftidan, uni hayratga soldi, chunki u faqat ta'zim qilmoqchi edi.

paras.en: As soon as he had gone — before opening the door he had leaned his shoulder against it for a moment and taken in the room with a look meant for no one in particular any more — K. said to the assistants: 'I'll fetch my notes from my room, then we'll discuss the next piece of work.' They wanted to come with him. 'Stay here!' said K. They still wanted to come. K. had to repeat the order even more sternly. In the hall Barnabas was no longer to be seen. But he had only just left.
paras.uz: U ketishi bilanoq — eshikni ochishdan oldin u yelkasi bilan eshikka biroz suyanib, endi hech kimga alohida qaratilmagan nigoh bilan xonani qamrab olgan edi — K. yordamchilarga dedi: «Xonamdan yozuvlarimni olib kelaman, keyin keyingi ishni muhokama qilamiz.» Ular u bilan birga bormoqchi bo'lishdi. «Qolinglar!» — dedi K. Ular hamon u bilan birga bormoqchi edilar. K. buyruqni yanada qattiqroq takrorlashga majbur bo'ldi. Dahlizda Barnabas endi yo'q edi. Lekin u hozirgina ketgan edi-ku.

paras.en: Yet in front of the house, too — fresh snow was falling — K. could not see him. He called: 'Barnabas!' No answer. Could he still be in the house? There seemed to be no other possibility. Nevertheless K. shouted the name once more with all his strength. The name thundered through the night. And from far away there did now come a faint answer. So Barnabas was already that far. K. called him back and at the same time went to meet him; where they met, they could no longer be seen from the inn.
paras.uz: Lekin uy oldida ham — yangi qor yog'ayotgan edi — K. uni ko'rmadi. U chaqirdi: «Barnabas!» Javob yo'q. Nahotki u hali uyda bo'lsa? Boshqa imkoniyat yo'qdek tuyulardi. Shunga qaramay K. ismni yana bir bor butun kuchi bilan baqirdi. Ism tun bo'ylab gumburlab yangradi. Va uzoqdan endi baribir zaif javob keldi. Demak, Barnabas allaqachon shunchalik uzoqqa ketgan ekan. K. uni qaytib chaqirdi va ayni paytda uning istiqboliga yurdi; ular uchrashgan joydan mehmonxona endi ko'rinmasdi.
