chapters.title: 4. Frieda's choice
chapters.recap_uz: K. peshtaxta ostida yashirinadi; Frida uni mehmonxona egasidan yashiradi. Ular tunni pivo ko'lmaklari orasida birga o'tkazadi. Klamm Fridani chaqirganda, u «Men yer o'lchovchining yonidaman!» deb javob beradi va Klammni tark etadi. Ular «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonaga ko'chishadi. K. Frida bilan turmush qurmoqchi ekanini aytadi, lekin avval Klamm bilan gaplashishni talab qiladi. Beka buni imkonsiz deydi va K.ni «hech kim», johil begona deb ataydi.

paras.en: But in the silence that had now suddenly fallen, K. heard footsteps from the hall. To secure himself somehow, he leaped behind the bar counter, under which was the only possible hiding place. True, he was not forbidden to be in the bar, but since he wanted to spend the night here, he had to avoid being seen now. So when the door really did open, he slipped under the counter. Being discovered there was not without danger either, of course; still, the excuse that he had hidden from the peasants gone wild would then not be unbelievable. It was the landlord. 'Frieda!' he called, and walked up and down the room a few times.
paras.uz: Lekin endi to'satdan cho'kkan sukunatda K. dahlizdan qadam tovushlarini eshitdi. O'zini qandaydir himoya qilish uchun u bufet peshtaxtasi orqasiga sakradi, uning ostida yashirinishning yagona imkoniyati bor edi. To'g'ri, bufetda bo'lish unga taqiqlanmagan edi, lekin u shu yerda tunamoqchi bo'lgani uchun hozir ko'rinib qolishdan saqlanishi kerak edi. Shuning uchun eshik haqiqatan ochilganida, u peshtaxta ostiga sirpanib kirdi. U yerda topilib qolish ham, albatta, xavfsiz emas edi, lekin baribir u holda quturgan dehqonlardan yashiringan edim, degan bahona ishonchsiz bo'lmasdi. Bu mehmonxona egasi edi. «Frida!» — chaqirdi u va xonada bir necha marta u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurdi.

paras.en: Fortunately Frieda soon came and did not mention K.; she only complained about the peasants and, in her effort to look for K., went behind the counter. There K. could touch her foot, and from then on he felt safe. Since Frieda did not mention K., the landlord finally had to. 'And where is the land surveyor?' he asked. He was in general a polite man, refined by constant and relatively free dealings with people far above him, but he spoke to Frieda in a particularly respectful way. This was striking chiefly because in talking he never stopped being an employer speaking to an employee — and a rather saucy employee at that. 'I'd quite forgotten the land surveyor,' said Frieda, and set her small foot on K.'s chest. 'He must have left long ago.' — 'But I didn't see him,' said the landlord, 'and I was in the hall nearly all the time.' — 'Well, he isn't here,' said Frieda coolly. 'Perhaps he has hidden,' said the landlord. 'From the impression he made on me, he's capable of anything.' — 'He would hardly have that much nerve,' said Frieda, and pressed her foot harder on K.
paras.uz: Baxtiga Frida tez keldi va K. haqida gapirmadi, faqat dehqonlardan shikoyat qildi va go'yo K.ni izlash maqsadida peshtaxta orqasiga o'tdi. U yerda K. uning oyog'iga tega oldi va shu paytdan boshlab o'zini xavfsiz his qildi. Frida K. haqida gapirmagani uchun, oxir-oqibat mehmonxona egasining o'zi gapirishiga to'g'ri keldi. «Yer o'lchovchi qayerda?» — so'radi u. U umuman olganda xushmuomala, o'zidan ancha yuqori turadiganlar bilan doimiy va nisbatan erkin muloqot tufayli nozik tarbiyalangan odam edi, lekin Frida bilan alohida hurmat bilan gaplashardi; bu ayniqsa ko'zga tashlanardi, chunki shunga qaramay suhbatda u xizmatchiga, buning ustiga ancha surbet xizmatchiga nisbatan ish beruvchiligini to'xtatmasdi. «Yer o'lchovchini butunlay unutibman», dedi Frida va kichkina oyog'ini K.ning ko'kragiga qo'ydi. «U allaqachon ketib qolgan bo'lsa kerak.» — «Lekin men uni ko'rmadim, — dedi mehmonxona egasi, — men deyarli butun vaqt dahlizda edim.» — «Bu yerda u yo'q», dedi Frida sovuqqina. «Balki yashiringandir, — dedi mehmonxona egasi, — undan olgan taassurotimga ko'ra, undan ko'p narsani kutish mumkin.» — «U bunchalik jur'atga bormasa kerak», dedi Frida va oyog'ini K.ga qattiqroq bosdi.

paras.en: There was something cheerful and free in her nature that K. had not noticed before at all, and it gained the upper hand quite improbably when, laughing suddenly, she said: 'Perhaps he's hidden down here,' bent down to K., kissed him fleetingly, jumped up again and said sadly: 'No, he isn't here.' But the landlord too gave cause for surprise when he now said: 'It is very awkward for me not to know for certain whether he has left. It's not only a question of Herr Klamm; it's a question of the rules. And the rules apply to you, Fräulein Frieda, just as to me. You are responsible for the bar; I'll search the rest of the house. Good night! Sleep well!' He could hardly have left the room before Frieda had switched off the electric light and was under the counter with K. 'My darling! My sweet darling!' she whispered, but did not touch K. at all; as if fainting with love she lay on her back and spread out her arms; time was surely endless before her happy love; she sighed rather than sang some little song. Then, because K. remained lost in silent thought, she started up and began tugging at him like a child: 'Come, one suffocates down here!'
paras.uz: Uning tabiatida K. avval umuman payqamagan qandaydir quvnoq, erkin narsa bor edi va u birdan kulib: «Balki u shu yerda, pastda yashiringandir», deb K.ga engashib, uni bir zum o'pib, yana sakrab turib, g'amgin: «Yo'q, u bu yerda yo'q», deganida, bu narsa aql bovar qilmas darajada ustun keldi. Lekin mehmonxona egasi ham endi shunday deganida hayratga sabab bo'ldi: «U ketganmi-yo'qmi, aniq bilmasligim menga juda noqulay. Gap faqat janob Klammda emas, gap qoidada. Qoida esa siz uchun ham, Frida xonim, men uchun ham amal qiladi. Bufet uchun siz javobgarsiz, uyning qolgan qismini men qidirib chiqaman. Xayrli tun! Yaxshi dam oling!» U xonadan hali chiqib ulgurmagan bo'lsa kerak, Frida allaqachon elektr chirog'ini o'chirib, peshtaxta ostida K.ning yonida edi. «Jonim! Shirin jonim!» — pichirladi u, lekin K.ga umuman tegmadi; go'yo muhabbatdan hushini yo'qotgandek chalqancha yotib, qo'llarini yoydi; uning baxtli muhabbati oldida vaqt cheksiz edi; u qandaydir kichik qo'shiqni kuylashdan ko'ra ko'proq xo'rsinardi. Keyin K. jim o'yga botib qolgani uchun cho'chib tushdi va uni boladek tortqilay boshladi: «Yur, bu yerda, pastda bo'g'ilib qolamiz-ku!»

paras.en: They put their arms round each other; the small body burned in K.'s hands. They rolled a few paces in a state of oblivion from which K. kept trying, in vain, to save himself; they thudded against Klamm's door and then lay among the little puddles of beer and the other rubbish that covered the floor. There hours passed — hours of breathing together, of hearts beating together, hours in which K. constantly felt that he was losing his way, or that he had gone further into a foreign land than any man before him, a foreignness in which even the air had nothing of the air of home, in which one must suffocate from strangeness and yet, among its senseless enticements, could do nothing but go on, go on losing one's way. And so, at least at first, it was no fright to him but a comforting dawning of awareness when from Klamm's room a deep, commanding, indifferent voice called for Frieda. 'Frieda,' said K. into Frieda's ear, passing on the call. With what was virtually an innate obedience Frieda wanted to jump up, but then she remembered where she was, stretched, laughed quietly and said: 'I'm surely not going to go — never shall I go to him.' K. wanted to object, wanted to urge her to go to Klamm, began to gather up the remains of her blouse; but he could say nothing; he was too happy to hold Frieda in his hands — too anxiously happy, too, for it seemed to him that if Frieda left him, everything he had would leave him.
paras.uz: Ular bir-birini quchoqlashdi, kichkina tana K.ning qo'llarida yonardi; ular K. doimo, lekin behuda qutulishga uringan bir hushsizlik ichida bir necha qadam yumalashdi, Klammning eshigiga g'ira urilishdi va keyin pol qoplangan kichik pivo ko'lmaklari va boshqa chiqindilar orasida yotib qolishdi. U yerda soatlar o'tdi — birga nafas olish, yuraklar birga urish soatlari; bu soatlarda K. doimo adashayotgandek yoki o'zidan oldin hech bir inson bormagan darajada begona yurtga borib qolgandek his qilardi — havosida ham vatan havosidan biror zarra bo'lmagan, begonalikdan bo'g'ilib qolish kerak bo'lgan va uning bema'ni vasvasalari orasida oldinga yurish, adashishda davom etishdan boshqa hech narsa qilib bo'lmaydigan begonalik. Shuning uchun, hech bo'lmaganda avvaliga, Klammning xonasidan chuqur, buyruqbozona-befarq ovoz Fridani chaqirganida, bu uning uchun dahshat emas, balki yupatuvchi bir hushga kelish edi. «Frida», dedi K. Fridaning qulog'iga va shu bilan chaqiruvni unga yetkazdi. Deyarli tug'ma itoatkorlik bilan Frida sakrab turmoqchi bo'ldi, lekin keyin qayerda ekanini esladi, cho'zildi, jimgina kuldi va dedi: «Men bormayman-ku, hech qachon uning oldiga bormayman.» K. unga qarshi gapirmoqchi, uni Klammning oldiga borishga undamoqchi bo'ldi, uning bluzkasidan qolgan parchalarni yig'ishtira boshladi, lekin hech narsa ayta olmadi; Fridani qo'llarida ushlab turganidan haddan tashqari baxtli edi, haddan tashqari xavotirli-baxtli ham, chunki unga agar Frida uni tashlab ketsa, borini hammasi uni tashlab ketadigandek tuyulardi.

paras.en: And as if strengthened by K.'s consent, Frieda clenched her fist, knocked with it on the door and called: 'I'm with the land surveyor! I'm with the land surveyor!' At that Klamm did fall silent. But K. got up, knelt beside Frieda and looked about him in the dim light before dawn. What had happened? Where were his hopes? What could he expect from Frieda now that everything had been betrayed? Instead of advancing with the utmost caution, as befitted the greatness of the enemy and of the goal, he had rolled about all night here in puddles of beer whose smell was now stupefying. 'What have you done?' he said to himself. 'We're both lost.' — 'No,' said Frieda, 'only I am lost; but I have won you. Be calm. But look how those two are laughing.' — 'Who?' asked K., and turned round. On the counter sat his two assistants, a little bleary from lack of sleep but cheerful — it was the cheerfulness that comes from faithful performance of duty. 'What do you want here?' shouted K., as though they were to blame for everything. He looked round for the whip Frieda had had in the evening. 'We had to look for you,' said the assistants, 'since you didn't come down to us in the taproom. Then we looked for you at Barnabas's and found you here at last. We've been sitting here all night.
paras.uz: Va go'yo K.ning roziligidan kuch olgandek, Frida mushtini tugib, u bilan eshikni taqillatdi va qichqirdi: «Men yer o'lchovchining yonidaman! Men yer o'lchovchining yonidaman!» Shunda Klamm, albatta, jim bo'lib qoldi. Lekin K. o'rnidan turdi, Fridaning yonida tiz cho'kdi va tong oldi g'ira-shirasida atrofga qaradi. Nima bo'ldi? Uning umidlari qayerda? Hamma narsa fosh bo'lgan ekan, endi u Fridadan nima kutishi mumkin? Dushman va maqsadning ulkanligiga mos ravishda eng katta ehtiyotkorlik bilan oldinga yurish o'rniga, u bu yerda butun tun pivo ko'lmaklarida ag'nab yotdi, ularning hidi endi kishini mast qilardi. «Nima qilding?» — dedi u o'z-o'ziga. «Ikkalamiz ham halok bo'ldik.» — «Yo'q, — dedi Frida, — faqat men halok bo'ldim, lekin seni qo'lga kiritdim. Tinchlan. Lekin qara, anavi ikkovi qanday kulyapti.» — «Kim?» — so'radi K. va o'girildi. Peshtaxta ustida uning ikki yordamchisi o'tirardi — biroz uyqusiz, lekin quvnoq; bu sodiqlik bilan burchni bajarishdan keladigan quvnoqlik edi. «Bu yerda nima qilyapsizlar?» — deb qichqirdi K., go'yo hamma narsaga ular aybdordek. U atrofda Frida kechqurun ushlab turgan qamchini izladi. «Seni izlashimiz kerak edi-ku, — deyishdi yordamchilar, — chunki sen pastga, umumiy zalga bizning oldimizga tushmading; keyin seni Barnabasnikidan izladik va nihoyat shu yerdan topdik. Butun tun shu yerda o'tiribmiz.

paras.en: It's no easy job, you know.' — 'I need you by day, not at night,' said K. 'Get out.' — 'But it is day now,' they said, and did not move. It really was day; the yard door was opened, and the peasants streamed in with Olga, whom K. had completely forgotten. Olga was as lively as in the evening, however badly her clothes and hair had suffered; already in the doorway her eyes were looking for K. 'Why didn't you come home with me?' she said, almost in tears. 'Because of a creature like that!' she said then, and repeated it several times. Frieda, who had disappeared for a moment, came back with a small bundle of linen. Olga stepped sadly aside. 'Now we can go,' said Frieda; it went without saying that she meant the Bridge Inn, where they were to go. K. with Frieda, the assistants behind them — that was the procession. The peasants showed great contempt for Frieda — naturally, since she had ruled them strictly until now; one of them even took a stick and pretended he would not let her go until she jumped over it; but her look was enough to drive him off. Outside in the snow K. breathed a little more freely. The happiness of being in the open air was so great that this time it made the difficulty of the way bearable; had K. been alone, he would have walked even better.
paras.uz: Xizmat oson emas-da.» — «Sizlar menga kunduzi kerak, kechasi emas, — dedi K., — yo'qolinglar.» — «Hozir kunduz-ku», deyishdi ular va qimirlashmadi. Haqiqatan ham kunduz edi, hovli eshigi ochildi, dehqonlar K. butunlay unutgan Olga bilan ichkariga yopirilib kirishdi. Kiyimlari va sochlari qanchalik buzilgan bo'lmasin, Olga kechqurungidek jonli edi, eshikdayoq uning ko'zlari K.ni izladi. «Nega men bilan uyga bormading?» — dedi u deyarli yig'lab. «Shunday bir xotin uchunmi!» — dedi u keyin va buni bir necha marta takrorladi. Bir lahzaga g'oyib bo'lgan Frida kichkina kir tugunchasi bilan qaytib keldi. Olga g'amgin chetga chiqdi. «Endi ketishimiz mumkin», dedi Frida; ular boradigan joy «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxona ekani o'z-o'zidan ayon edi. Frida bilan K., ularning orqasida yordamchilar — mana shunday karvon. Dehqonlar Fridaga katta nafrat ko'rsatishdi — bu tabiiy edi, chunki u hozirgacha ularni qattiq boshqarib kelgan edi; hatto biri tayoq olib, go'yo u tayoq ustidan sakramaguncha uni qo'yib yubormoqchi emasdek qildi; lekin uning nigohi uni haydash uchun yetarli bo'ldi. Tashqarida, qorda K. biroz yengil nafas oldi. Ochiq havoda bo'lish baxti shunchalik katta ediki, bu safar u yo'lning qiyinligini ham chidasa bo'ladigan qildi; agar K. yolg'iz bo'lganida, yanada yaxshiroq yurgan bo'lardi.

paras.en: At the inn he went straight to his room and lay down on the bed; Frieda made up a bed for herself on the floor beside it. The assistants had pushed their way in too and were driven out, but then came back in through the window. K. was too tired to drive them out again. The landlady came up specially to greet Frieda and was called 'little mother' by her; there was an incomprehensibly warm greeting, with kisses and long embraces. There was little peace in the little room anyway; the maids too often came clumping in in their men's boots to bring or fetch something. If they needed something from the bed, which was stuffed with all sorts of things, they pulled it out from under K. without consideration. They greeted Frieda as one of their own. In spite of this commotion K. stayed in bed the whole day and the whole night. Frieda looked after his small needs. When at last he got up the next morning, very refreshed, it was already the fourth day of his stay in the village. He would have liked to talk to Frieda privately, but the assistants — with whom, by the way, Frieda now and then joked and laughed too — prevented him by their mere obtrusive presence. They were not demanding, it is true; they had settled down in a corner on the floor on two old skirts.
paras.uz: Mehmonxonada u darhol xonasiga borib, karavotga yotdi, Frida esa uning yonida polga o'ziga joy hozirladi. Yordamchilar ham ichkariga bostirib kirishgan edi, ularni haydashdi, lekin keyin ular deraza orqali yana kirib kelishdi. K. ularni yana haydash uchun juda charchagan edi. Mehmonxona bekasi Frida bilan salomlashish uchun ataylab yuqoriga chiqdi, Frida uni «onajon» deb atadi; o'pishlar va uzoq quchoqlashishlar bilan tushunib bo'lmas darajada samimiy salomlashish bo'ldi. Kichkina xonada umuman tinchlik kam edi; xizmatkor qizlar ham erkak etiklarida tez-tez taraq-turuq qilib biror narsa olib kelish yoki olib ketish uchun kirib turishardi. Agar ularga turli narsalar bilan tiqilib ketgan karavotdan biror narsa kerak bo'lsa, uni K.ning ostidan beparvolik bilan tortib olishardi. Fridani ular o'zlariga tengdek salomlashishdi. Bu tashvishga qaramay K. butun kun va butun tun karavotda qoldi. Kichik yumushlarini Frida bajarib turdi. Ertasi kuni ertalab u juda tetiklashib, nihoyat o'rnidan turganida, bu allaqachon uning qishloqda bo'lishining to'rtinchi kuni edi. U Frida bilan yolg'iz gaplashishni istardi, lekin yordamchilar — aytgancha, Frida ular bilan ba'zan hazillashib, kulib ham turardi — faqat o'zlarining surbet borligi bilan bunga xalaqit berishardi. To'g'ri, ular talabchan emas edilar: ular bir burchakda polda ikkita eski ayol yubkasi ustiga joylashib olishgan edi.

paras.en: It was their ambition, as they discussed with Frieda, not to disturb the land surveyor and to take up as little room as possible. In this regard they made various attempts, always with lisping and giggling: they crossed arms and legs, crouched down together, and in the twilight one saw in their corner only one big tangle. Yet unfortunately one knew from experience by daylight that they were very attentive observers, always staring across at K., whether in apparently childish play they used their hands as telescopes and got up to similar nonsense, or merely blinked across and seemed chiefly busy tending their beards, which mattered a great deal to them and which they compared countless times for length and fullness and had Frieda judge.
paras.uz: Ular Frida bilan gaplashganidek, ularning orzusi janob yer o'lchovchini bezovta qilmaslik va imkon qadar kam joy egallash edi; ular bu jihatdan, albatta doim shivirlab va pixillab kulib, turli urinishlar qilishardi: qo'l va oyoqlarini chalishtirishar, birga g'ujanak bo'lib olishardi, g'ira-shirada ularning burchagida faqat bitta katta chigal ko'rinardi. Shunga qaramay, afsuski, kunduzgi tajribadan ma'lum ediki, ular juda diqqatli kuzatuvchilar edi, doim K.ga tikilib turishardi — xoh go'yo bolalarcha o'yinda qo'llarini durbin qilib, shunga o'xshash bema'ni ishlar qilishsin, xoh shunchaki ko'z qisib qarab, asosan soqollarini parvarish qilish bilan band bo'lgandek ko'rinishsin; soqollar ular uchun juda muhim edi, ularni son-sanoqsiz marta uzunligi va qalinligi bo'yicha bir-biri bilan solishtirishar va Fridaga baholatishardi.

paras.en: Often, from his bed, K. watched the doings of the three with complete indifference.
paras.uz: K. ko'pincha karavotidan uchovining qiliqlarini butunlay befarqlik bilan kuzatib yotardi.

paras.en: When he now felt strong enough to leave the bed, they all hurried up to wait on him. He was not yet strong enough to resist their services; he noticed that he was thereby falling into a certain dependence on them that could have bad consequences, but he had to let it happen. Nor was it at all unpleasant to drink at the table the good coffee Frieda had fetched, to warm himself at the stove Frieda had lit, to let the assistants, in their zeal and clumsiness, run up and down the stairs to bring washing water, soap, comb and mirror, and finally — because K. had uttered a faint wish that could be so interpreted — a little glass of rum too.
paras.uz: Endi u karavotdan turishga yetarlicha kuchli ekanini his qilganida, hammasi unga xizmat qilish uchun shoshib kelishdi. U hali ularning xizmatlariga qarshilik qila oladigan darajada kuchli emas edi; buning orqali ularga ma'lum darajada qaram bo'lib qolayotganini, bu yomon oqibatlarga olib kelishi mumkinligini payqadi, lekin bunga yo'l qo'yishga majbur edi. Buning ustiga, stol yonida Frida olib kelgan yaxshi qahvani ichish, Frida yoqqan pechkada isinish, yordamchilarni g'ayrat va epsizlik bilan yuvinish suvi, sovun, taroq va ko'zgu, oxirida esa — K. shunday tushunish mumkin bo'lgan sekin bir istak bildirgani uchun — bir qadahcha rom olib kelish uchun zinadan yugurib tushib-chiqishga qo'yib berish umuman unchalik yoqimsiz emas edi.

paras.en: In the midst of this commanding and being served, K. said, more from a comfortable mood than in any hope of success: 'Now go away, you two. I need nothing more for the moment and want to talk to Fräulein Frieda alone.' And as he did not exactly see resistance on their faces, he added, to make it up to them: 'Then the three of us will go to the mayor; wait for me downstairs in the taproom.' Strangely, they obeyed, only saying before they left: 'We could wait here too.' And K. answered: 'I know, but I don't want you to.'
paras.uz: Bu buyruq berish va xizmat ko'rish o'rtasida K. muvaffaqiyatga umid qilishdan ko'ra ko'proq rohatbaxsh kayfiyatdan dedi: «Endi ketinglar, ikkovingiz, hozircha menga boshqa hech narsa kerak emas, Frida xonim bilan yolg'iz gaplashmoqchiman.» Va ularning yuzlarida aniq qarshilik ko'rmagach, ularni ovutish uchun yana dedi: «Keyin uchovimiz oqsoqolning oldiga boramiz, meni pastda, zalda kutinglar.» G'alati, ular bo'ysunishdi, faqat ketishdan oldin: «Biz shu yerda ham kutishimiz mumkin edi», deyishdi. K. esa javob berdi: «Bilaman, lekin buni istamayman.»

paras.en: It was annoying to K., but in a certain sense welcome too, when Frieda, who had sat down on his lap as soon as the assistants had gone, said: 'What have you got against the assistants, darling? We needn't have any secrets from them. They are faithful.' — 'Oh, faithful,' said K. 'They lie in wait for me constantly; it's senseless, but loathsome.' — 'I think I understand you,' she said, and hung on his neck, and wanted to say something more but could not go on; and because the chair stood right beside the bed, they swayed over and fell onto it. There they lay, but not as abandoned as that night. She was searching for something and he was searching for something; furiously, making faces, boring their heads into each other's breasts, they searched, and their embraces and their tossing bodies did not make them forget but reminded them of the duty to search. As dogs scratch desperately at the ground, so they scratched at each other's bodies; and helplessly, disappointed, to snatch a last happiness, their tongues sometimes passed broadly over each other's faces. Only tiredness made them still and grateful to each other. Then the maids came up as well. 'Look how they're lying here,' said one, and out of pity threw a cloth over them.
paras.uz: Yordamchilar ketishi bilanoq uning tizzasiga o'tirgan Frida: «Jonim, yordamchilarga nima qarshiliging bor? Ulardan sir saqlashimiz shart emas. Ular sodiq», deganida, bu K.ning jahlini chiqardi, lekin qaysidir ma'noda yoqimli ham edi. — «Eh, sodiq, — dedi K., — ular meni doimo poylashadi, bu ma'nosiz, lekin jirkanch.» — «Seni tushunaman, shekilli», dedi u va uning bo'yniga osildi, yana nimadir demoqchi bo'ldi, lekin gapira olmadi; kreslo shundoqqina karavot yonida turgani uchun ular u tomonga chayqalib, yiqilishdi. U yerda yotishdi, lekin o'sha tundagidek berilib emas. U nimanidir izlardi va u nimanidir izlardi; g'azab bilan, yuzlarini burishtirib, boshlarini bir-birining ko'kragiga tiqib izlashardi va ularning quchoqlashishlari, tipirchilayotgan tanalari ularni unuttirmas, aksincha, izlash burchini eslatardi; itlar umidsizlik bilan yerni tirnaganidek, ular ham bir-birining tanasini tirnashardi; va ojiz, ko'ngli qolgan holda, so'nggi baxtni olish uchun ba'zan tillari bilan bir-birining yuzini keng yalashardi. Faqat charchoq ularni jim va bir-biriga minnatdor qildi. Keyin xizmatkor qizlar ham yuqoriga chiqishdi. «Qara, bular bu yerda qanday yotishibdi», dedi biri va achinib ularning ustiga bir mato tashladi.

paras.en: When K. later freed himself from the cloth and looked about him, the assistants — this did not surprise him — were back in their corner, pointing at K. with their fingers, urging each other to be serious, and saluting. But besides them, the landlady was sitting right by the bed, knitting a stocking — a small piece of work that hardly suited her enormous figure, which almost darkened the room. 'I have been waiting a long time,' she said, and raised her broad face, lined with many wrinkles of age but in its great mass still smooth, perhaps once beautiful. The words sounded like a reproach, an inappropriate one, for K. had not asked her to come. So he merely confirmed her words with a nod and sat up. Frieda stood up too, but left K. and leaned against the landlady's chair. 'Could what you want to tell me not wait, Frau Landlady,' said K. absently, 'until I come back from the mayor's? I have an important meeting there.' 'This one is more important, believe me, land surveyor,' said the landlady. 'There it's probably only a matter of work, but here it's a matter of a human being — of Frieda, my dear maid.' — 'Oh, I see,' said K., 'then of course; only I don't know why this matter isn't left to the two of us.' — 'Out of love, out of concern,' said the landlady, and drew to her Frieda's head — Frieda, standing, reached only to the shoulder of the seated landlady.
paras.uz: Keyinroq K. matodan bo'shanib, atrofga qaraganida, yordamchilar — bu uni hayron qoldirmadi — yana o'z burchaklarida edilar, barmoqlari bilan K.ni ko'rsatib, bir-birini jiddiy bo'lishga undashar va harbiycha salom berishardi; lekin bundan tashqari, karavotning shundoqqina yonida mehmonxona bekasi o'tirib, paypoq to'qiyotgan edi — xonani deyarli qorong'ilashtirib turgan ulkan gavdasiga unchalik mos kelmaydigan kichik bir ish. «Uzoq vaqtdan beri kutyapman», dedi u va ko'p ajinlar bilan kesilgan, lekin katta hajmida hali silliq, ehtimol bir vaqtlar chiroyli bo'lgan keng yuzini ko'tardi. So'zlar ta'nadek, nojo'ya ta'nadek eshitildi, chunki K. uning kelishini so'ramagan edi. Shuning uchun u faqat bosh irg'ab uning so'zlarini tasdiqladi va to'g'rilanib o'tirdi. Frida ham turdi, lekin K.ni tashlab, bekaning kreslosiga suyandi. «Bekam, — dedi K. parishon holda, — menga aytmoqchi bo'lgan gapingizni oqsoqolning oldidan qaytgunimcha qoldirib bo'lmaydimi? U yerda muhim uchrashuvim bor.» «Bunisi muhimroq, ishoning, janob yer o'lchovchi, — dedi beka, — u yerda gap, ehtimol, faqat ish haqida, bu yerda esa gap bir inson haqida — Frida, mening aziz xizmatkorim haqida.» — «Ha, shundaymi, — dedi K., — unda, albatta; faqat bu ishni nega ikkovimizga qoldirishmasligini bilmayman.» — «Muhabbatdan, g'amxo'rlikdan», dedi beka va tik turganida o'tirgan bekaning faqat yelkasiga yetadigan Fridaning boshini o'ziga tortdi.

paras.en: 'Since Frieda has such confidence in you,' said K., 'I can't do otherwise either. And since Frieda called my assistants faithful only a little while ago, we are all friends among ourselves. So I can tell you, Frau Landlady, that I think it best if Frieda and I marry, and very soon. Unfortunately, unfortunately, I shall not be able to make up to Frieda what she has lost through me — her position at the Herrenhof and Klamm's friendship.' Frieda raised her face; her eyes were full of tears, and nothing triumphant was in them. 'Why me? Why was I of all people chosen for this?' — 'What?' asked K. and the landlady at the same time. 'She's confused, the poor child,' said the landlady, 'confused by the meeting of too much happiness and unhappiness.' And as if to confirm these words, Frieda now threw herself on K., kissed him wildly as though there were no one else in the room, and then, weeping and still holding him, fell on her knees before him. While K. stroked Frieda's hair with both hands, he asked the landlady: 'You seem to agree with me?'
paras.uz: — Frida sizga bunchalik ishonar ekan, — dedi K., — men ham boshqacha qila olmayman. Frida hozirgina yordamchilarimni sodiq deb atagani uchun, demak, hammamiz o'zaro do'stmiz. Unda sizga, bekam, aytishim mumkinki, men Frida bilan turmush qurishimizni, buning ustiga juda tez orada qurishimizni eng yaxshisi deb hisoblayman. Afsus, afsuski, men bu bilan Frida men tufayli yo'qotgan narsani — «Herrenhof»dagi o'rnini va Klammning do'stligini — o'rniga qo'ya olmayman. — Frida yuzini ko'tardi, ko'zlari yoshga to'la edi, ularda g'oliblikdan asar ham yo'q edi. — Nega men? Nega aynan men bunga tanlandim? — Nima? — deb bir vaqtda so'rashdi K. va beka. — U sarosimada, bechora bola, — dedi beka, — haddan tashqari ko'p baxt va baxtsizlik birga kelganidan sarosimada. — Va go'yo bu so'zlarni tasdiqlagandek, Frida endi K.ga otildi, xonada boshqa hech kim yo'qdek uni ehtiros bilan o'pdi va keyin yig'lab, hamon uni quchoqlagan holda, uning oldida tiz cho'kdi. K. ikki qo'li bilan Fridaning sochini silarkan, bekadan so'radi: — Siz menga qo'shilayotgandek ko'rinasiz?

paras.en: 'You are a man of honour,' said the landlady; there were tears in her voice too, she looked a little wasted and was breathing heavily; nevertheless she still found the strength to say: 'Now we shall only have to think of certain guarantees you must give Frieda; for however great my respect for you is now, you are still a stranger, you can refer to no one, your domestic circumstances are unknown here. So guarantees are necessary — you will see that, my dear land surveyor; after all, you yourself stressed how much Frieda is losing by her connection with you.' — 'Certainly, guarantees, naturally,' said K. 'They will probably best be given before a notary, but other authorities of the Count's may perhaps interfere as well. Besides, I too have something I absolutely must settle before the wedding. I must speak to Klamm.' — 'That's impossible,' said Frieda, raising herself a little and pressing herself against K. 'What an idea!' — 'It must be done,' said K. 'If it is impossible for me to arrange, you must do it.' — 'I can't, K., I can't,' said Frieda. 'Klamm will never talk to you. How can you even think that Klamm will talk to you!' — 'And would he talk to you?' asked K. 'No, not either,' said Frieda, 'not with you, not with me; these are sheer impossibilities.'
paras.uz: — Siz sharafli odamsiz, — dedi beka, uning ovozida ham ko'z yoshi bor edi, u biroz holsizlangandek ko'rinar va og'ir nafas olardi; shunga qaramay, yana gapirishga kuch topdi: — Endi faqat Fridaga berishingiz kerak bo'lgan ba'zi kafolatlar haqida o'ylash kerak bo'ladi, chunki sizga bo'lgan hurmatim qanchalik katta bo'lmasin, siz baribir begonasiz, hech kimga tayana olmaysiz, oilaviy ahvolingiz bu yerda noma'lum. Demak, kafolatlar zarur, buni tushunasiz, aziz janob yer o'lchovchi, axir Frida siz bilan bog'lanish orqali qanchalik ko'p narsa yo'qotayotganini o'zingiz ta'kidladingiz-ku. — Albatta, kafolatlar, tabiiy, — dedi K., — ularni notarius oldida bergan ma'qulroq bo'lsa kerak, lekin balki boshqa graflik idoralari ham aralashar. Aytgancha, men ham to'ydan oldin albatta bir ishni hal qilishim kerak. Men Klamm bilan gaplashishim kerak. — Bu mumkin emas, — dedi Frida biroz ko'tarilib va K.ga yopishib, — qanday fikr! — Shunday bo'lishi kerak, — dedi K. — Agar men buni uddalay olmasam, sen qilishing kerak. — Qila olmayman, K., qila olmayman, — dedi Frida, — Klamm sen bilan hech qachon gaplashmaydi. Klamm sen bilan gaplashadi, deb qanday o'ylay olasan! — Sen bilan gaplasharmidi? — so'radi K. — U ham yo'q, — dedi Frida, — na sen bilan, na men bilan, bular sof imkonsizliklar.

paras.en: She turned to the landlady with outspread arms: 'Just look, Frau Landlady, what he is asking.' 'You are peculiar, land surveyor,' said the landlady, and it was frightening how she sat up more erect now, her legs planted apart, her mighty knees pushing out through her thin skirt. 'You are asking the impossible.' — 'Why is it impossible?' asked K. 'I'll explain that to you,' said the landlady, in a tone as if this explanation were not a last kindness but already the first punishment she was handing out. 'I'll gladly explain it to you. I don't belong to the Castle, true, and I am only a woman, and only a landlady here, in an inn of the lowest class — it isn't of the lowest class, but not far from it — and so it may be that you don't attach much importance to my explanation. But I have kept my eyes open in my life, and I have met many people, and I have carried the whole burden of the business alone; for my husband is a good lad, but an innkeeper he is not, and what responsibility is he will never grasp. You, for instance, owe it only to his carelessness — I was ready to drop with tiredness that evening — that you are here in the village at all, that you are sitting here on the bed in peace and comfort.' — 'What?' asked K., waking from a certain absent-mindedness, excited more by curiosity than by annoyance.
paras.uz: U qo'llarini yoyib, bekaga o'girildi: «Qarang-chi, bekam, u nima talab qilyapti.» «Siz g'alati odamsiz, janob yer o'lchovchi», dedi beka va u endi qanday tikroq o'tirgani — oyoqlarini kerib, yupqa yubka orqali ulkan tizzalarini oldinga chiqarib — qo'rqinchli edi. «Siz imkonsiz narsani talab qilyapsiz.» — «Nega imkonsiz?» — so'radi K. «Buni sizga tushuntiraman, — dedi beka go'yo bu tushuntirish so'nggi iltifot emas, balki u berayotgan birinchi jazodek ohangda, — buni sizga bajonidil tushuntiraman. To'g'ri, men Qasrga tegishli emasman, faqat ayolman va faqat bekaman, bu yerda eng past darajadagi mehmonxonada — eng past darajada emas, lekin undan uzoq ham emas — shuning uchun mening tushuntirishimga ko'p ahamiyat bermasligingiz mumkin, lekin men hayotimda ko'zlarimni ochiq tutganman, ko'p odamlar bilan uchrashganman va xo'jalikning butun og'irligini yolg'iz ko'targanman, chunki erim yaxshi bola-yu, lekin mehmonxona egasi emas, mas'uliyat nima ekanini hech qachon tushunmaydi. Masalan, siz bu yerda, qishloqda ekaningiz, shu yerda, karavotda tinch va rohatda o'tirganingiz uchun faqat uning beparvoligidan qarzdorsiz — o'sha oqshom men charchoqdan yiqilish darajasida edim.» — «Qanday?» — so'radi K. qandaydir parishonlikdan uyg'onib, g'azabdan ko'ra ko'proq qiziqishdan hayajonlanib.

paras.en: 'You owe it only to his carelessness!' cried the landlady again, her forefinger pointed at K. Frieda tried to calm her. 'What do you want?' said the landlady, turning her whole body quickly. 'The land surveyor asked me and I must answer him. How else is he to understand what is self-evident to us: that Herr Klamm will never speak to him — what am I saying, "will": can never speak to him. Listen, land surveyor! Herr Klamm is a gentleman from the Castle; that in itself, quite apart from Klamm's position otherwise, means a very high rank. But what are you, whose consent to marry we are so humbly seeking here? You are not from the Castle, you are not from the village, you are nothing. Unfortunately, though, you are something after all — a stranger, someone superfluous and in the way everywhere, someone who constantly causes trouble, on whose account the maids have to be moved out, someone whose intentions are unknown, who has seduced our dearest little Frieda and to whom, unfortunately, we must give her as a wife. For all that I don't really reproach you. You are what you are; I have seen too much in my life not to be able to bear this sight as well. But now just imagine what you are actually asking. A man like Klamm is to speak to you!
paras.uz: «Faqat uning beparvoligidan qarzdorsiz!» — deb yana qichqirdi beka ko'rsatkich barmog'ini K.ga qaratib. Frida uni tinchlantirishga urindi. «Nima istaysan, — dedi beka butun gavdasi bilan tez o'girilib. — Janob yer o'lchovchi mendan so'radi va men unga javob berishim kerak. Aks holda u biz uchun o'z-o'zidan ayon bo'lgan narsani — janob Klamm u bilan hech qachon gaplashmasligini, nima deyapman, «gaplashmasligini»: hech qachon gaplasha olmasligini qanday tushunadi? Eshiting, janob yer o'lchovchi! Janob Klamm — Qasr janobi, bu o'z-o'zidan, Klammning boshqa mavqeidan qat'i nazar, juda yuqori martaba degani. Siz-chi, biz bu yerda turmushga roziligini shunchalik kamtarlik bilan so'rayotgan siz kimsiz? Siz Qasrdan emassiz, qishloqdan emassiz, siz hech kimsiz. Lekin afsuski, siz baribir kimdirsiz — begona, ortiqcha va hamma joyda yo'lda turgan odam, u tufayli doimo tashvish chekiladigan, u tufayli xizmatkor qizlarni boshqa joyga ko'chirish kerak bo'ladigan odam, niyatlari noma'lum odam, bizning eng aziz kichkina Fridamizni yo'ldan urgan va afsuski, unga xotinlikka berishimiz kerak bo'lgan odam. Bularning hammasi uchun men sizni aslida ayblamayman. Siz qanday bo'lsangiz, shundaysiz; men hayotimda shunchalik ko'p narsani ko'rganmanki, bu manzaraga ham chiday olaman. Lekin endi aslida nima talab qilayotganingizni tasavvur qiling. Klamm kabi odam siz bilan gaplashishi kerak emish!

paras.en: It hurt me to hear that Frieda let you look through the peephole; even when she did that she had already been seduced by you. Tell me, how did you bear the sight of Klamm at all? You needn't answer, I know — you bore it very well. You are not even capable of really seeing Klamm; that is no arrogance on my part, for I myself am not capable of it either. Klamm is to speak to you — but he doesn't even speak to people from the village; never yet has he spoken in person to anyone from the village. It was Frieda's great distinction — a distinction that will be my pride to the end of my days — that he at least used to call out Frieda's name, and that she could speak to him when she liked and was granted the peephole; but even with her he did not speak. And that he sometimes called Frieda need not have the meaning one would like to give it at all; he simply called out the name "Frieda" — who knows his intentions? That Frieda naturally came running was her affair, and that she was let in to him without objection was Klamm's kindness; but that he actually summoned her, one cannot claim. Of course, now even what there was is gone for ever.
paras.uz: Frida sizga tirqishdan qarashga ruxsat berganini og'riq bilan eshitdim, buni qilganidayoq u siz tomonidan yo'ldan urilgan edi. Ayting-chi, Klammni ko'rishga umuman qanday chidadingiz? Javob berishingiz shart emas, bilaman, juda yaxshi chidadingiz. Siz Klammni haqiqatan ko'rishga umuman qodir emassiz, bu mening takabburligim emas, chunki men o'zim ham bunga qodir emasman. Klamm siz bilan gaplashishi kerak emish, lekin u hatto qishloq odamlari bilan ham gaplashmaydi, hali hech qachon qishloqdan biror kishi bilan o'zi gaplashmagan. Uning hech bo'lmaganda Fridaning ismini chaqirib turishi, Frida xohlagan paytda u bilan gaplasha olishi va tirqishga ruxsat olgani — bu Fridaning katta sharafi edi, bu sharaf umrimning oxirigacha mening faxrim bo'lib qoladi; lekin u bilan ham u gaplashmagan. Uning ba'zan Fridani chaqirgani ham unga berishni istagan ma'noga ega bo'lishi shart emas, u shunchaki «Frida» degan ismni aytgan — uning niyatlarini kim biladi? — Fridaning, albatta, shoshib kelgani uning ishi edi, uning qarshiliksiz uning oldiga kiritilgani Klammning marhamati edi, lekin u uni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri chaqirgan, deb da'vo qilib bo'lmaydi. Albatta, endi bo'lgan narsa ham abadiy yo'qoldi.

paras.en: Perhaps Klamm will still call out the name "Frieda" — that is possible — but she will certainly not be let in to him any more, a girl who has taken up with you. And there is one thing, just one thing, that I cannot understand with my poor head: that a girl who was said to be Klamm's mistress — a much exaggerated term, by the way, in my opinion — should let you so much as touch her.'
paras.uz: Balki Klamm hali «Frida» ismini aytar, bu mumkin, lekin siz bilan aloqa qilgan qizni u endi o'zining oldiga, albatta, kiritmaydi. Va faqat bir narsani, faqat bir narsani bechora boshim bilan tushuna olmayman: Klammning ma'shuqasi deyilgan qiz — aytgancha, men buni juda mubolag'ali atama deb hisoblayman — sizga o'ziga hatto tegishga ham ruxsat bergani.»

paras.en: 'Certainly, that is strange,' said K., and took Frieda onto his lap — she submitted at once, though with lowered head — 'but it proves, I think, that other things too are not quite as you believe. For instance, you are certainly right when you say that before Klamm I am nothing; and if I now still ask to speak to Klamm and am not dissuaded even by your explanations, that does not yet mean that I can so much as bear the sight of Klamm without a door in between, or that I won't run out of the room the moment he appears. But such a fear, however justified, is no reason for me not to risk it. And if I succeed in standing my ground before him, then it is not at all necessary that he speak to me; it is enough for me to see the impression my words make on him; and if they make none, or if he doesn't even hear them, I still have the gain of having spoken freely before a powerful man. But you, Frau Landlady, with your great knowledge of life and of people, and Frieda, who only yesterday was Klamm's mistress — I see no reason to abandon that word — can surely easily get me an opportunity to speak to Klamm; if it is possible no other way, then at the Herrenhof; perhaps he is still there today.'
paras.uz: — Albatta, bu g'alati, — dedi K. va boshini egib bo'lsa ham darhol bo'ysungan Fridani tizzasiga oldi, — lekin bu, menimcha, boshqa narsalar ham siz o'ylaganingizdek aynan shunday emasligini isbotlaydi. Masalan, Klamm oldida men hech kimman, deganingizda, albatta, haqsiz; va agar men hozir Klamm bilan gaplashishni talab qilsam va hatto sizning tushuntirishlaringiz ham meni bundan qaytarmagan bo'lsa, bu hali men Klammni oramizda eshik bo'lmagan holda ko'rishga chiday olaman, yoki u paydo bo'lishi bilanoq xonadan qochib chiqmayman, degani emas. Lekin bunday, garchi asosli bo'lsa ham, qo'rquv men uchun baribir ishga jur'at qilmaslikka sabab emas. Agar uning oldida bardosh bera olsam, unda u men bilan gaplashishi umuman shart emas, so'zlarim unga qanday taassurot qoldirganini ko'rsam kifoya; agar hech qanday taassurot qoldirmasa yoki u ularni umuman eshitmasa ham, baribir qudratli odam oldida erkin gapirganimdan foyda ko'raman. Lekin siz, bekam, hayot va odamlarni katta bilishingiz bilan, va kechagina Klammning ma'shuqasi bo'lgan Frida — bu so'zdan voz kechishga sabab ko'rmayapman — menga Klamm bilan gaplashish imkoniyatini, albatta, osongina topib bera olasiz; agar boshqa yo'l bilan mumkin bo'lmasa, «Herrenhof»da, balki u bugun ham hali o'sha yerdadir.

paras.en: 'It is impossible,' said the landlady, 'and I see that you lack the ability to understand it. But tell me, what do you want to speak to Klamm about?' — 'About Frieda, of course,' said K.
paras.uz: — Bu mumkin emas, — dedi beka, — va ko'ryapmanki, sizda buni tushunish qobiliyati yetishmaydi. Lekin ayting-chi, Klamm bilan nima haqida gaplashmoqchisiz? — Frida haqida, albatta, — dedi K.

paras.en: 'About Frieda?' asked the landlady uncomprehendingly, and turned to Frieda. 'Do you hear, Frieda? About you he wants — he! — to speak with Klamm, with Klamm!' 'Oh,' said K., 'you are such a clever, awe-inspiring woman, Frau Landlady, and yet every little thing frightens you. Well then, I want to speak to him about Frieda — that is not so monstrous, rather a matter of course. For you are surely mistaken too if you think that from the moment I appeared Frieda became of no importance to Klamm. You underestimate him if you think so. I feel very well that it is presumptuous of me to want to instruct you in this respect, but I must do it all the same. Nothing in Klamm's relation to Frieda can have been changed by me. Either there was no essential relation — that is really what those people say who deny Frieda the honourable name of mistress — and in that case there is none today either; or else there was one, and then how could it be disturbed by me, who am, as you rightly said, a nothing in Klamm's eyes? One believes such things in the first moment of fright, but the slightest reflection must set it right. But let us let Frieda give her own opinion on this.' With her gaze wandering into the distance and her cheek against K.'s breast, Frieda said: 'It is surely as little mother says: Klamm wants nothing more to do with me. But not, of course, because you came, darling; nothing of that kind could have shaken him. But I do believe it was his doing that we found each other there under the counter. Blessed, not cursed, be that hour.' — 'If that is so,' said K. slowly — for Frieda's words were sweet, and he closed his eyes for a few seconds to let them soak into him — 'if that is so, there is even less reason to fear a talk with Klamm.'
paras.uz: «Frida haqidami?» — so'radi beka tushunmay va Fridaga o'girildi. «Eshityapsanmi, Frida, u sen haqingda, u, Klamm bilan, Klamm bilan gaplashmoqchi.» «Eh, — dedi K., — siz, bekam, shunday aqlli, hurmat uyg'otadigan ayolsiz, lekin har bir arzimas narsa sizni qo'rqitadi. Mayli, men u bilan Frida haqida gaplashmoqchiman, bu unchalik dahshatli emas, aksincha, o'z-o'zidan tushunarli. Chunki agar men paydo bo'lgan lahzadan boshlab Frida Klamm uchun ahamiyatsiz bo'lib qoldi, deb o'ylasangiz, albatta, adashasiz. Agar shunday o'ylasangiz, uni kam baholaysiz. Bu jihatdan sizga dars bermoqchi bo'lishim takabburlik ekanini yaxshi his qilaman, lekin baribir buni qilishim kerak. Men tufayli Klammning Fridaga munosabatida hech narsa o'zgarmagan bo'lishi kerak. Yo hech qanday muhim munosabat bo'lmagan — Fridadan ma'shuqa degan faxriy nomni olib qo'yadiganlar aslida shuni aytishadi — unda u bugun ham yo'q; yoki u bo'lgan, unda qanday qilib men tufayli — siz to'g'ri aytganingizdek, Klamm ko'zida hech kim bo'lgan men tufayli — buzilishi mumkin? Bunday narsalarga qo'rquvning birinchi lahzasida ishoniladi, lekin eng kichik mulohaza ham buni to'g'rilashi kerak. Aytgancha, Fridaga bu haqda o'z fikrini aytishga imkon beraylik.» Nigohi uzoqlarga ketgan holda, yuzini K.ning ko'kragiga qo'yib, Frida dedi: «Albatta, onajon aytganidek: Klamm endi men haqimda hech narsa bilishni istamaydi. Lekin, albatta, sen, jonim, kelganing uchun emas, bunday narsa uni larzaga keltira olmasdi. Lekin menimcha, biz o'sha yerda, peshtaxta ostida topishganimiz uning ishi; o'sha soat la'natlanmasin, muborak bo'lsin.» — «Agar shunday bo'lsa, — dedi K. sekin, chunki Fridaning so'zlari shirin edi, u so'zlar uni butunlay qamrab olishi uchun bir necha soniya ko'zlarini yumdi, — agar shunday bo'lsa, Klamm bilan gaplashishdan qo'rqishga yanada kamroq sabab bor.»

paras.en: 'Truly,' said the landlady, looking down at K. from on high, 'you sometimes remind me of my husband; you are as defiant and childish as he is. You've been in the place a couple of days and already you want to know everything better than the natives — better than me, an old woman, and better than Frieda, who has seen and heard so much at the Herrenhof. I don't deny that it is possible, once in a while, to achieve something quite against the rules and against tradition. I have never experienced anything of the kind, but there are said to be examples; very well. But then it certainly doesn't happen the way you go about it, constantly saying "No, no", swearing only by your own head and ignoring the most well-meant advice. Do you think my concern is for you? Did I bother about you as long as you were alone? Though it would have been good, and much could have been avoided. The only thing I said to my husband about you at that time was: "Keep away from him." That would still hold for me today, if Frieda had not now been dragged into your fate. It is to her that you owe — whether you like it or not — my care, and even my attention. And you may not simply turn me away, because you are strictly answerable to me, the only one who watches over little Frieda with a mother's care. It may be that Frieda is right and everything that has happened is Klamm's will; but of Klamm I now know nothing; I shall never speak to him, he is utterly out of my reach. But you are sitting here, holding my Frieda, and are yourself — why should I keep quiet about it? — held by me. Yes, held by me; for just try, young man, if I turn you out of the house, to find a place to stay anywhere in the village — even if it were a dog kennel.'
paras.uz: «Rostini aytsam, — dedi beka va K.ga yuqoridan pastga qaradi, — siz ba'zan menga erimni eslatasiz, siz ham u kabi qaysar va bolalarchasiz. Qishloqda bir necha kundan beri yuribsiz-u, allaqachon hamma narsani mahalliy odamlardan, men kampirdan va «Herrenhof»da shunchalik ko'p narsani ko'rgan va eshitgan Fridadan yaxshiroq bilmoqchisiz. Men qoidalarga va qadimiy odatlarga butunlay zid biror narsaga ham bir kun erishish mumkinligini inkor etmayman; men bunday narsani boshdan kechirmaganman, lekin aytishlaricha, bunga misollar bor, bo'lishi mumkin; lekin unda bu, albatta, siz qilayotgan tarzda — doimo «Yo'q, yo'q» deb, faqat o'z boshingga qasam ichib, eng xayrixoh maslahatlarni ham eshitmay — sodir bo'lmaydi. Nima, mening g'amxo'rligim sizga qaratilgan deb o'ylaysizmi? Siz yolg'iz bo'lgan paytingizda siz bilan qiziqqanmidim? Garchi bu yaxshi bo'lardi va ko'p narsadan saqlanish mumkin edi. O'shanda erimga siz haqingizda aytgan yagona gapim: «Undan uzoqroq yur», edi. Agar Frida endi sizning taqdiringizga tortilmaganida, bu men uchun bugun ham amalda bo'lardi. Sizga bo'lgan g'amxo'rligim, hatto e'tiborim uchun — yoqsa ham, yoqmasa ham — siz undan qarzdorsiz. Va siz meni shunchaki rad eta olmaysiz, chunki kichkina Frida ustida onalik g'amxo'rligi bilan qo'riqchilik qilayotgan yagona odam — menga qattiq javobgarsiz. Balki Frida haqdir va sodir bo'lgan hamma narsa Klammning irodasidir; lekin men endi Klamm haqida hech narsa bilmayman; men u bilan hech qachon gaplashmayman, u men uchun butunlay yetib bo'lmasdir; siz esa shu yerda o'tirib, mening Fridamni ushlab turibsiz va o'zingiz — nega buni yashiray? — men tomonimdan ushlab turilibsiz. Ha, men tomonimdan, chunki urinib ko'ring-chi, yigit, agar sizni uydan haydasam, qishloqning biror joyida boshpana topishga, hatto bu it kulbasi bo'lsa ham.»

paras.en: 'Thank you,' said K. 'Those are frank words, and I believe you completely. So my position is as uncertain as that, and with it Frieda's position too.'
paras.uz: — Rahmat, — dedi K., — bu ochiq so'zlar va men sizga to'liq ishonaman. Demak, mening ahvolim, shuningdek, u bilan bog'liq ravishda Fridaning ahvoli ham shunchalik ishonchsiz ekan.

paras.en: 'No!' the landlady broke in furiously. 'Frieda's position has nothing whatever to do with yours in this respect. Frieda belongs to my house, and nobody has the right to call her position here uncertain.'
paras.uz: — Yo'q! — deb g'azab bilan gapini bo'ldi beka. — Fridaning ahvoli bu jihatdan sizniki bilan umuman bog'liq emas. Frida mening uyimga tegishli va hech kim uning bu yerdagi ahvolini ishonchsiz deb atashga haqli emas.

paras.en: 'Very well, very well,' said K., 'I'll grant you that too, especially as Frieda, for reasons unknown to me, seems too afraid of you to interfere. Let us keep for the moment only to me, then. My position is highly uncertain — you don't deny it; on the contrary, you are at pains to prove it. As with everything you say, this too is for the most part right, but not entirely. For instance, I know of a quite good place to sleep that is open to me.'
paras.uz: — Yaxshi, yaxshi, — dedi K., — bunda ham sizga qo'shilaman, ayniqsa Frida menga noma'lum sabablarga ko'ra aralashish uchun sizdan juda qo'rqayotganga o'xshaydi. Unda hozircha faqat men haqimda gaplashaylik. Mening ahvolim juda ishonchsiz, siz buni inkor etmaysiz, aksincha, isbotlashga harakat qilyapsiz. Siz aytgan hamma narsa kabi, bu ham katta qismi bo'yicha to'g'ri, lekin butunlay emas. Masalan, men uchun ochiq bo'lgan ancha yaxshi tunash joyini bilaman.

paras.en: 'Where? Where?' cried Frieda and the landlady, so simultaneously and so eagerly, as if they had the same motives for asking. — 'At Barnabas's,' said K.
paras.uz: — Qayerda? Qayerda? — deb qichqirishdi Frida va beka shunchalik bir vaqtda va shunchalik ishtiyoq bilanki, go'yo ularning savolining sabablari bir xil edi. — Barnabasnikida, — dedi K.
